abilities.name: Solar Flare Sky Chi
abilities.description: Aurora's ultimate Sky Chi power, unleashing a massive solar flare.

trivia: Solar Flare Aurora is a counterpart of Aurora in Skylanders: Imaginators.
She is the niece of Master Eon.
She used the alias 'Boss Blades McSlashinator' to study swordplay and combat arts in secret.
Her English voice actor is Britt Baron, credited as Brittany Uomoleale.
Master Eon eventually admitted that her secret alias, 'Boss Blades McSlashinator', sounded 'pretty cool'.

sonic-boom.name: Sonic Boom
sonic-boom.description: Sonic Boom is a black and blue griffin in Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure. She is part of the Air element.
sonic-boom.biography: Long ago, Sonic Boom took refuge high atop a mountain peak in the far reaches of Skylands, hoping to keep her griffin hatchlings safe. But despite her precautions, a devious wizard tracked her down and placed a wicked curse on the griffin eggs. Once hatched, the young hatchlings can live for only mere moments before they magically return to their shells... only to be hatched again in an endless cycle. Wanting to prevent such evil from happening to others, Sonic Boom joined the Skylanders and has trained her young to defend Skylands each time they are hatched.
sonic-boom.personality: Sonic Boom is described as the maternal individual of the Skylanders since she and her young are the only Skylanders who fight evil as a family. As protective as only a mother can be, maternal Sonic Boom shelters all who need help beneath her wings. She also dislikes bullying. Sonic Boom can also be sensitive, as demonstrated in Terrafin Battles the Boom Brothers when she looked hurt after Terrafin yelled at the griffin in order to get through Sonic Boom's screeching.
sonic-boom.gameplay: Sonic Boom has the ability to shoot sonic waves from her mouth at her enemies. She can also toss out her eggs and her hatchlings will emerge out of their eggshells to attack surrounding enemies and follow Sonic Boom around for a short while, and they can also grow over time, improving their damage output, and a later upgrade lets them develop wings to help their movement speed increase. After a while, they magically return to their eggshells due to the wizard's curse and must be released from their eggs again before repeating the attacking process. The babies also return to their eggshells when damaged enough, ready to be hatched again. Enemies will also try to target the babies as well, so Sonic Boom can use them to set them up for a roar attack. With the Medea Griffin path, her babies become more powerful. Her first upgrade, Sunny Side Up, allows her to summon all three babies at once and also use the actual eggs to knock away opponents, making it easier for her roar to damage them. The second upgrade, Sibling Rivalry, allows her to summon a fourth baby, further increasing the possible damage output. Her final upgrade, Terrible Twos, has her babies hatch at their maximum strength, giving them the speed benefit in the beginning, as well as giving them a faster attack speed. In summary, this path makes her babies much effective at distracting or even defeating opponents, letting her deal with individual enemies more easily. With the Siren Griffin path, her roar becomes more effective. Her first upgrade, Echolocation, creates a sound wave wherever a roar hits an enemy, damaging nearby opponents. Since she can move while roaring, she can create multiple shockwaves that can hit clustered enemies multiple times. Her second upgrade, Egg Shocker, has her create a shockwave that knocks opponents away if her roar hits an egg. Finally, her third upgrade, More Boom!, lets her charge up a massive sound wave that hits all around her for massive damage. In summary, this path increases Sonic Boom's crowd control ability; she not only gains a relatively quick attack that can clear opponents surrounding her, but her roar allows her defeat entire clusters of enemies more easily. Her Wow Pow allows her hatchlings to merge into a larger, and more powerful griffin baby which can exist at the same time as the other babies if they are thrown out afterward, while her Soul Gem allows her to increase the damage output and range of her hatchlings. In Terrafin Battles the Boom Brothers, it is stated that Sonic Boom's roar is powerful enough to knock down trees and even dislodge mountains.

trivia: Sonic Boom will occasionally vocally make a caw or squawk sound. If her babies are around, they will respond back!
If Sonic Boom is at full health, her babies will eat nearby food, and get both larger and more powerful.
Sonic Boom's eyes are yellow in-game and in her trailer, but in toy form, they are green. However, in Giants, her eyes are greenish-yellow in the game.
Her Roar attack can light up purple Tzo Crystals, but it can't destroy them.

Her Wow Pow power, Super Baby, resembles a Gryphon/T-Rex hybrid as it walks on two legs, has tiny forearms, and a large head. Unlike her regular babies, the Super Baby only lasts about 1 minute before it has to be summoned again.
If you have purchased Resonant Frequency, roaring at the Super Baby gives it the ability to release a circular roar, damaging all enemies around it.

The Wizard's curse may have actually given her griffin babies a form of immortality, as they return to their eggshells after a short time, and hatch out young again, never to grow old, and they also return when dealt heavy damage, to hatch again as if nothing happened.
Sonic Boom is one of many Skylanders who can spawn helpers (others include Warnado, Terrafin, Double Trouble, Hot Head, Pop Fizz, Zoo Lou, Bat Spin, and Turbo Charge Donkey Kong).
She speaks with a British accent.
Her upgrade path 'Medea Griffin' alludes to the mythical Greek sorceress Medea, who was the wife of Jason.
Some fans mistake Sonic Boom for a Dragon. Due to not being voiced in Spyro's Adventure, some fans mistook her as male. Which is odd considering she lays eggs that hatch chicks.
Sonic Boom's quote 'Breaking the barrier!' is a reference to her name, as a sonic boom is created by breaking the sound barrier.
In her Series 2 figure form, Sonic Boom has a baby griffin by her side. She and Double Trouble are the only two Skylanders whose Series 2 figure forms have little helpers by their sides.
She bears a great resemblance to a Verreaux's Eagle.
Her catchphrase is a play on the phrase 'Full Steam Ahead!' and 'Full Speed Ahead!'.
While on promotional art she looks dark blue, Sonic Boom looks black and navy blue in toy form.
She is missing her armour in most of her upgrade pictures in Spyro's Adventure.
Sonic Boom is one of the few mothers in the Skylanders series (another includes Kaos' Mom).

spitfire.name: Spitfire
spitfire.description: Spitfire is a flame spirit who is the leader of the SuperChargers in Skylanders: SuperChargers. His signature vehicle is the Hot Streak, and along with it, Spitfire comes with most of the non-Nintendo console Starter Packs of the game.
spitfire.biography: Spitfire was on pace to become the fastest driver in the Super Skylands Racing Circuit. With his lightning quick reflexes and nerves of steel, this tech enhanced flame spirit was absolutely unbeatable. But during the championship event at Skywinder Canyon, he was illegally bumped off course by a goblin racer and sent flying into the canyon wall in a fiery explosion! Most thought that this would put an end his racing career. But three weeks later, he was back on the track, more fired up than ever to claim the title. Unfortunately, it was then that all of Skylands fell under the rule of Kaos in his Sky Eating machine, and the racing came to an end. That's when Spitfire was approached by Master Eon with an offer that could get him back behind the wheel as the new leader of an elite driving team – the Skylander Superchargers!
spitfire.personality: Spitfire is a spirited speed demon with lightning quick reflexes and nerves of steel. He is quite arrogant and overconfident, though the comics show Spitfire will keep it aside to act like a proper leader. He might be unbeatable, but Spitfire is no hothead. His bravery, determination and tenacity make him a fiery force to be reckoned with.
spitfire.gameplay: Spitfire can punch enemies with his flaming claws, spin quickly to summon a Flamenado, and dash forward with a flash of his fire at great speeds. In Skylanders: Battlecast, he is shown to have some additional skills. Spitfire can direct his tornado of fire forward through his claws as a Torchnado, summon the Hot Streak set on Auto Fire temporarily and a burning wheel that costs less the more he cast beforehand, and drink Nitromethane for a temporary attack and spell boost.

trivia: Spitfire is the only leader of an elite team of Skylanders to be of the Fire element.
He also bears a resemblance to the Fire Viper from Skylanders: Swap Force.
He seems to resemble The Darkness at the end of Skylanders: SuperChargers, and his face also resembles the Sky Eater.
He has similarities to Sonic the Hedgehog, as both characters are blue, very fast, and have a boastful attitude.

He is voiced by Diedrich Bader, who voices Hoss Delgado from The Grim Adventures of Billy and Mandy, Batman in Batman: The Brave and the Bold, Warp Darkmatter in Buzz Lightyear of Star Command, Hundun in Kung Fu Panda: Legends of Awesomeness and Kraven the Hunter in Ultimate Spider-Man.
He is the only SuperCharger without legs.
He is also the only SuperCharger without any weaponry.
As seen in Battlecast, Spitfire can drink vehicle fuel.
He is one of the three Skylanders to have 'Fire' (his element) in his name (the other two are Fire Kraken and Wildfire).
He shares the lowest HP stat of the series with Trigger Happy.

Spitfire is the only new SuperChargers Skylander to appear in the starter pack. The other Starter Pack Skylanders appeared in previous games (Stealth Elf from Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure and Donkey Kong and Bowser from their own decades-old franchises).
The term spitfire refers to someone who has a fiery temperament. This name was also used for a plant in Skylanders: Universe.
Mighty Magiswords creator, Kyle A. Carrozza, was once asked to design some prototype swords for possible commercial tie-ins, including a Skylanders/Spitfire-inspired Magisword.
Early in development, Spitfire went through a number of alternate concept designs, including a version without armor, a feminine-looking counterpart, and a version in which his body was colored gold.

splat.name: Splat
splat.description: Splat is a pink faun who is one of the two Magic SuperChargers in Skylanders: SuperChargers. Her signature vehicle is the Splatter Splasher.
splat.biography: Splat grew up in a typical faun village, which was perfectly manicured and orderly. Every day in school, she and her classmates would recite the same poems, play the same music, and paint the same picture – which was always a portrait of their great ancestor, Fluty Hoofdancer. But this didn't suit Splat. The only art she wanted to learn was the art of war! After school, she would sneak off to the river and practice her own free form fighting technique against Chompies and other creatures that were causing trouble. When the elder fauns learned of this, they were outraged. But soon thereafter, a band of Drow attacked the village to steal their valuable art, and while the other fauns cowered in fear, Splat stood her ground. Unleashing her self-taught fighting style, she defended her village and sent the Drow running. Now as a member of the Skylanders, Splat makes quite the impression wherever she goes!
splat.personality: Although Splat was in boredom of doing repetitive work at school, she is still a colorful character and admires her various artwork. She also encourages others to break free of their comfort zones and express themselves with paintings. She also knows how to make an excellent impression on her peers. She is the definition of spunky; she's got a lot of fight in her and rarely backs down from a ruckus. Splat is also known to be quite brave when duty calls.
splat.gameplay: Splat can pummel enemies with her paintbrush staff as well as lob blobs of paint. She can also summon billy goat-like inklings to charge forward and leave pools of ink that damage her opponents.

trivia: Her catchphrase is based on Sun Tzu's Chinese military text called The Art of War.
While Splat's eyes are purple in her promotional art, her eyes are green in the game and in toy form.
Her nose is pink in toy form and in her promotional art, but it is black in the game.
Splat's name, her methods of attack, and her inkling creations strongly resemble the gameplay mechanics of the game Splatoon.
Her name early in development, Oil Pan, is a pun on the object and the faun god of the wilds in Greek Mythology.
Certain toy figures of Splat have been reported to possess a faint, sweet vanilla-like scent.
Splat's voice actress, Brittany Snow is best known for her roles as Amber Von Tussle in Hairspray and Chloe in the Pitch Perfect trilogy.
Her stats phrase 'Picture perfect' may be a reference to Snow's role in the latter films.
In Skylanders: Ring of Heroes, Splat's outfit was changed from the waist up and parts of her hair are longer, for reasons unknown.

spotlight.name: Spotlight
spotlight.description: Spotlight is a white dragon who is the Light Core Skylander in Skylanders: Trap Team.
spotlight.biography: Spotlight was discovered by Master Eon in the Prismatic Palace, where the Portal Master had ventured seeking the Crystal Orb of Light. Upon finding the Orb, Eon reached out and gently touched it - causing a brilliant light to emanate in all directions. Having been infused with Eon's magic, the Orb glowed magnificently. And when Eon slowly lowered his hand from his shielded eyes, Spotlight stood before him in a respectful bow. Her power of Light was unknown to him, for it was not of the eight common Elements in Skylands. But sensing that the Ancients sent Spotlight to him for a reason, he took her to the Core of Light and trained her to defend it as a member of the Skylanders. And when none other than evil Portal Master Kaos destroyed it - Spotlight vanished!
spotlight.personality: Spotlight is a respectful and loyal dragon who was chosen by the Ancients to defend the Core of Light. She carries herself with dignity, showing a deep sense of duty toward Master Eon and the safety of Skylands.
spotlight.gameplay: Spotlight can shoot powerful eyebeams and throw golden halo rings that reflect the eye lasers onto enemies. Spotlight can summon a pillar of heavenly energy to erupt from the ground which damages foes near it. Her Soul Gem allows her to create other light dragons from the heavenly aura when zapped with her eyebeams.

abilities.description: Shoot a Heavenly Aura with Eye Beams to power it up and do more damage.

abilities.name: Light It Up
abilities.description: Eye Beams do even MORE damage and have longer range.

abilities.name: Bling
abilities.description: Shoot two Halo Rings at once.

abilities.name: Heavy Halo
abilities.description: Halo Rings are larger and do more damage.

abilities.name: Ring Shot
abilities.description: Halo Rings shoot light beams of their own.

abilities.name: Uplifting Experience
abilities.description: Light enemies caught in Halo Rings up with the Heavenly Aura.

trivia: Spotlight is the only core Skylander of the Light Element as of Imaginators.

Her attack pattern is similar to Flashwing, as both Skylanders use light-based attacks. Both dragon Skylanders also share few battle phrases, including one that is Spotlight's catchphrase, 'Time to Shine!' and 'Outshining the rest!'
Spotlight also has a very similar play style to Prism Break, where both Skylanders fire beams and summon items (rings for Spotlight and crystals for Prism Break) to refract said beams.
She and Aurora are the only female Light Skylanders.
Spotlight's battle cry 'See the light!' is shared by Knight Light's catchphrase 'See the Light!'.
Spotlight and Knight Light are the only Light Skylanders to bear the Light Element symbol.

She is generally considered a Light counterpart to the Dark Skylander Blackout, considering they are both Dragons, both the only core Skylander of their element within Trap Team, and were both released alongside the Trap Masters of the same elements, being Knight Light and Knight Mare respectively.
She is relatively similar to Star Strike: Both of their attacks are linked with light, they both possess featureless eyes, and they are both voiced by Misty Lee.
One of her 3DS upgrades, Spotlight, shares the same name as her.
There is a glitch in which, after using Spotlight for a while, her 'Light Dragons' power stops working. To remedy this, Spotlight must be removed from the portal, then placed back onto it.
She and Drobot are both dragons that use eye beams.
Like Flashwing, Echo, Whirlwind and Cynder, Spotlight is a female dragon with no visible teeth.

springtime-trigger-happy.name: Springtime Trigger Happy
springtime-trigger-happy.description: Springtime Trigger Happy is an Easter-themed counterpart of Trigger Happy in Skylanders: Swap Force.
springtime-trigger-happy.biography: Every year the residents of Skylands gather together for the annual Dragon Egg Hunt, celebrating the arrival of spring time. In his enthusiasm for the event, Trigger Happy has dyed himself and his rocket in the pastel colors of the season. Now disguised as a dragon egg, his new mission is to end up in the basket of a lucky kid... and not a dragon!
springtime-trigger-happy.personality: Trigger Happy is highly enthusiastic about seasonal events, particularly the annual Dragon Egg Hunt, going as far as to disguise himself as a dragon egg in hopes of being found by a lucky child.
springtime-trigger-happy.gameplay: Springtime Trigger Happy uses Tech-based weaponry such as Gold Coin Shooters and Safe Cracker Bombs. He shares the same move set as Series 3 Trigger Happy, allowing him to throw Pots O' Gold and unleash a Coinsplosion.

abilities.name: Gold Coin Shooters
abilities.description: Shoots gold coins at enemies.

abilities.name: Safe Cracker Bomb
abilities.description: Throws safe cracker bombs that explode on impact.

abilities.name: Golden Super Charge
abilities.description: A powerful super-charged attack using golden energy.

abilities.name: Coinsplosion
abilities.description: A massive explosion of coins that damages all nearby enemies.

abilities.name: Pot O' Gold
abilities.description: Throws a pot of gold that causes significant damage.

trivia: To help go along with the Dragon Egg hunt, Trigger Happy also painted his rocket in the colors of the season.
Springtime Trigger Happy is one of three holiday based alter-ego Skylanders to come with an exclusive hat, the other two being Jolly Bumble Blast, and Kickoff Countdown.
They were also only released in Swap Force.
Springtime Trigger Happy comes with a unique hat for Swap Force, the Springtime Hat.
Springtime Trigger Happy, Hoppity Pop Fizz, Rocky Egg Roll, Eggsellent Weeruptor, and Eggcited Thrillipede are the only Easter Skylanders.
There is a flocked figure of Springtime Trigger Happy, which is the only case of a variant of a variant.

sprocket.name: Sprocket
sprocket.description: Sprocket is a goldling with red hair, featureless white eyes, and red lips. She wears blue and gold armor with a brown long sleeved shirt and pants underneath. She has blue mechanic goggles with green lenses on her head. She also wields a wrench.
sprocket.biography: Sprocket was raised with all the privileges of a rich, proper Goldling. But she cared little for fancy things. Instead, she spent most of her time growing up in her uncle's workshop, learning how to build and fix his many mechanical inventions. But everything changed on the day her uncle mysteriously vanished. When she eventually discovered that Kaos had been behind his disappearance, she constructed a battle suit and went after him, leaving the luxury and comfort of her family's wealth behind. From that moment on, Sprocket was dedicated to fighting the forces of evil, whilst never losing hope that she would reunite with her beloved uncle.
sprocket.personality: Resourceful, Sprocket isn't one to sit back and let others do the work. She jumps in with both armored feet, creating solutions for every problem imaginable.
sprocket.gameplay: Sprocket uses both brains and brawn in battle. She can smack foes with her large wrench and build machine gun turrets very quickly that lock on to enemies automatically and shoot them. She can also deploy special mines that bounce in the air before exploding when enemies are near. Sprocket can even hop into her turrets which becomes a battle tank, where she can shoot enemies. In Terrafin battles the Boom Brothers, it is shown that she has a laser cutter in her battle suit which can easily cut through metal. Her skills in technology are far greater, as she was able to repair the escape pod on Trash Mountain very quickly.

abilities.name: Wrench Whack
abilities.description: Press the Attack 1 button to swing the big wrench.

abilities.name: Turret Gun-O-Matic
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 to build a turret that shoots enemies. Climb inside by facing the turret and pressing Attack 2.

abilities.name: Auto Turret V2
abilities.description: Turret Gun-o-Matic does increased damage and has more HP.

abilities.name: Bouncing Betty Mines
abilities.description: Press Attack 3 to toss mines that explode when enemies are near.

abilities.name: 2 Times The Turrets
abilities.description: Can have 2 active turrets at once.

abilities.name: Tanks A Lot!
abilities.description: When climbing inside a turret, it transforms into a drivable assault tank.

abilities.name: Landmine Golf
abilities.description: Facing a mine, press Attack 1 to send it flying towards enemies.

abilities.name: Tanks for the New Toy
abilities.description: While driving a tank, hold Attack 2 to fire a Tesla Cannon. Turrets and Tank do increased damage.

abilities.name: Sprocket Combos
abilities.description: Press Attack 1, Hold Attack 2 for Power Surge. Press Attack 1, Attack 1, Hold Attack 3 for Mines O' Plenty

abilities.name: Monkey Wrench
abilities.description: Better wrench does increased damage.

abilities.name: All Mines
abilities.description: Sprocket can now deploy three Bouncing Betty mines at once.

abilities.name: Mine Drop!
abilities.description: While driving a tank, press Attack 3 to drop mines out of the back.

abilities.name: Exploding Shells
abilities.description: Turret and Tank shells now explode on contact, doing extra damage.

abilities.name: Self Destruct System
abilities.description: When a Turret or Tank expires, it detonates and damages anything nearby.

trivia: A sprocket is a wheel with teeth, similar to a gear, which meshes with others of its kind through chains or tracks (like those on a bicycle).
If Sprocket sets up a turret near Octavius in The Oracle, it will fire at him.

In the alpha version of Skylanders: Giants, Sprocket went by the placeholder names of Engineer and Spark. She originally appeared as an elf instead of a Goldling, and therefore had green skin, pointed ears, and pupilless white eyes.
Activision ordered her original catchphrase 'Fear the gear!' to be cut, as it sounded too much like Fright Rider's catchphrase.
Sprocket is voiced by E.G. Daily, best known for the voice of Buttercup in The Powerpuff Girls, Tommy Pickles in Rugrats, and Julius in Julius Jr.
She and Chill are the only Skylanders so far who don't have any basic upgrades for their primary attacks.
Her Monkey Wrench upgrade adds +6 to damage in Swap Force.
In her first artwork, Sprocket wore green goggles. But in both Giants and Swap Force, her goggles are black.
Sprocket is one of the few Skylanders to use a vehicle for an attack (others include Fryno, Starcast, and Tread Head).
She is the first female Tech Skylander in the series (the second being Gearshift).
She, Fright Rider and Hot Dog are the only Giants-debut core Skylanders without any LightCore counterparts.
During Giants's early development, Sprocket's abilities/upgrades were differently named, such as 'Wrench Whack' being called 'Wrench Attack' and 'Turret Gun-O-Matic' being called 'Auto Turret'.

spry.name: Spry
spry.description: Spry is the Mini counterpart of the Magic Skylander, Spyro in Skylanders: Trap Team.
spry.biography: The Skylander Minis started off as regular 'Sidekicks', assisting the Skylanders on many exciting adventures. And what they lacked in size they more than made up for in courage. Ultimately determined to become full-fledged heroes, they trained at the Skylands Academy - honing their powers and skills until they were ready. Now, they stand side by side with their full grown counterparts, ready to defend Skylands against Kaos and his evil minions.
spry.personality: Spry is an eager young dragon who wants to fight evil whenever he can. He's good at learning things quickly, which is a very important part of teamwork. He can be a little impulsive from time to time, but that's just because he loves being a hero so much.
spry.gameplay: In the games, Spry functions as a Mini character. He shares the same moveset as Spyro, utilizing fire breath for long-range attacks and horn charges for melee. He is characterized by his smaller stature and high agility compared to full-sized Skylanders.

abilities.name: Fire Breath
abilities.description: Spry shoots a stream of fire from his mouth.

abilities.name: Horn Charge
abilities.description: Spry charges forward with his horns.

abilities.name: Dragon Flight
abilities.description: Spry takes to the skies to avoid attacks and strike from above.

abilities.name: Triple Shot
abilities.description: Fire Breath shoots three fireballs instead of one.

abilities.name: Fire Shield
abilities.description: Spry surrounds himself with a protective shield of fire.

abilities.name: Fire Path
abilities.description: Enhances Fire Breath attacks for maximum fire damage.

abilities.name: Charge Path
abilities.description: Enhances Horn Charge attacks for faster and more powerful charges.

trivia: In the game, Spry's spines are completely purple.
In the 3DS version, he calls himself 'Spyro' instead of 'Spry'.
Paul Reiche stated that he thinks that Spry is Spyro's little brother or cousin. This statement doesn't match with the Miniverse. It's possible that Spyro views Spry as an little brother or cousin.
In Skylanders: SuperChargers, Spry seems to be the only Mini who doesn't have his voice pitched up.
Spry's eyes are so big, it takes him twice as long to blink.
Despite his regular counterpart having a different voice actor in Imaginators, Spry's voice remains unchanged, making him the only mini to have a unique voice.
Before Trap Team, Spry was originally planned to be a sidekick in Spyro's Adventure. He shares this designation with Bop.

spy-rise.name: Spy Rise
spy-rise.description: Spy Rise is a spider-like SWAP Force Skylander in Skylanders: Swap Force. His SWAP Force Ability is Climb.
spy-rise.biography: From the moment he could crawl, Spy Rise wanted nothing more than to join his father in the family business as a private investigator. But after being hired by a shadowy figure to gather information on the Cloudbreak Islands, his father vanished, leaving Spy Rise alone to search for answers. He scoured the land for clues, using his immense skill in reconnaissance to track down his missing father, but all roads came up empty. Then one day, he received a tip from none other than Master Eon, which led him to a hidden lair near Mt. Cloudbreak, where he not only found his long lost father, but also uncovered an evil plot to take control of the magical volcano during the next eruption ceremony. With his father safe, Spy Rise decided to pursue a new career -- as a member of the Skylanders.
spy-rise.personality: Spy Rise never gives up. The persistent P.I. sticks with a job until everything's wrapped up.
spy-rise.gameplay: Spy Rise's gameplay revolves around his unique spider-like mechanical body. His top half utilizes a 'Spyder Blaster' for ranged combat and a 'Spyder Scanner' to identify enemy weaknesses, while his bottom half provides high mobility through the 'Climb' ability and the use of 'Spyder Mines' and foot-mounted lasers/flamethrowers. In the console version, his stats start with 270 Health, 43 Speed, 18 Armor, 8 Critical Hit, and 25 Elemental Power.

abilities.name: Spyder Blaster
abilities.description: Press Attack 1 to shoot 3 Spyder projectiles that slow any enemies it hits.

abilities.name: Spyder Climb
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 to climb into the air with electro web, dropping back down will damage nearby enemies.

abilities.name: Spyder Scanner S3
abilities.description: Hold Attack 3 for a short time to scan enemies, release to shoot a high-powered laser. Fully scanned enemies take additional damage.

abilities.name: Spyder Sting
abilities.description: Press Attack 1 next to an enemy with low health to sting them and steal some health!

abilities.name: Future Tech
abilities.description: Super Spy Scanner S3 and Spyder Blaster do increased damage.

abilities.name: Spyder Mine
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 to climb into the air and drop a Spyder mine that will seek out and explode on nearby enemies.

abilities.name: Spyder Mine 002
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 to climb into the air, dropping two Spyder mines at once.

abilities.name: Rapid Laser Legs V17
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 to climb into the air, Hold Attack 2 while in the air to drop down and shoot electric bolts at enemies.

abilities.name: Spy with a Golden Hand
abilities.description: Gain a new golden blaster that shoots five projectiles at once.

abilities.name: Omega Sky Laser
abilities.description: Hold Attack 1 while in the sky to shoot down a massive laser that stuns enemies.

abilities.name: Cocoon Spinner
abilities.description: Hold Attack 1 to shoot a stream of web projectiles that slow and cocoon enemies.

abilities.name: Experimental Webs
abilities.description: Cocoon Spinner does increased damage. The experiment seems to be going well!

abilities.name: Electroweb Pulse Bomb
abilities.description: Hold Attack 1 to charge a web bomb, release to throw it which damages and slows enemies in a larger area.

abilities.name: Improved EPB
abilities.description: Electroweb Pulse Bomb does increased damage and has a larger explosion.

abilities.name: Foot-Mounted Flame
abilities.description: Hold Attack 2 to shoot flames from the feet, damaging any enemies that come too close.

abilities.name: Blue Flame
abilities.description: Flamethrower deals increased damage. Experimental feet fuel turns flames blue!

abilities.name: Pulse Cannon
abilities.description: Hold Attack 2 to charge a laser blast, release to shoot a massive wave of energy at enemies.

abilities.name: Advanced Pulse Cannon
abilities.description: Increase damage of pulse cannon. At least this one isn't experimental, right?

trivia: Spy Rise's bottom half is capable of avoiding damage from bombs and mines as well as wiping them out while performing Spyder Climb.
He and Wash Buckler are the only two SWAP Force Skylanders with a Climb Ability.

Spy Rise is ambidextrous, as demonstrated whenever he uses his Spyder Shooter and Spyder Scanner S3 with his left hand whereas he uses his right one for the Spyder Sting, Cocoon Spinner and/or Electroweb Pulse Bomb.
He is the only Skylander capable of measuring enemies' health bars, with his Spyder Scanner S3. The only other toy with this ability is the Sun Runner.
When he performs the Spyder Climb, he is capable of wiping out explosive mines without receiving damage. He can also avoid getting hit by enemies and bosses.
While standing still, he sneezes, making his goggles fall onto his face and obscuring his eyes until he lifts them back onto his forehead.
If you look really closely at Spy Rise's left hand while using Cocoon Spinner, it is quite similar to how Spider-Man shoots a web from the Marvel Comics.
Spy Rise is voiced by J.B. Blanc, who also voices Hood Sickle.
He and Blast Zone are the only Swap Force Skylanders to not wear a belt.
If he has Boom Jet's legs, he is called Spy Jet, the shortest name of all the SWAP Force combinations.
His Spyder Scanner S3 is a pun on the Samsung Galaxy S3.
He is one of the few Swap Force Skylanders to not have any counterparts or variants. The others are Boom Jet, Stink Bomb, Trap Shadow, Doom Stone and Rubble Rouser.
He and Dr. Krankcase are similar in the following ways: Both are Tech-elemental characters, both have range weapons, both have spider-like legs, and both have goggles on their foreheads.
His name is a play on 'high rise'.
The name of Spy Rise's top half 'Spy' is the shortest of all the SWAP Force's top halves, having only three letters.

spyro.name: Spyro
appearances: Gill Grunt and the Curse of the Fish Master
Stump Smash Crosses the Bone Dragon
Trigger Happy Targets the Evil Kaos
spyro.description: Spyro is a purple dragon who is the titular character of Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure, and a Core Skylander in the franchise. He is one of the three Skylanders that come with the console version starter pack of Spyro's Adventure, the other two being Gill Grunt and Trigger Happy. Additionally, he has Dark, Legendary, and Eon's Elite counterparts. His Series 3 counterpart is called Mega Ram Spyro.
spyro.biography: Spyro hails from a rare line of magical purple dragons that come from a faraway land few have ever traveled. It's been said that the Scrolls of the Ancients mention Spyro prominently -- the old Portal Masters having chronicled his many exciting adventures and heroic deeds. Finally, it was Master Eon himself who reached out and invited him to join the Skylanders. Now calling Skylands his home, Spyro remains one of its most valued protectors, with evil facing a new enemy -- and the Skylanders gaining a valued ally.
spyro.personality: Although eager and young at heart, Spyro is a strong-willed dragon who is fearless and brave; a born hero dedicated to defending his world from all things evil. He holds a photographic memory, and as a result, has encyclopedic knowledge of all the islands and creatures in Skylands he has encountered, more so than any other Skylander. He is always up for adventure (his favorite kind being treasure hunts), and is the first Skylander to leap into action. Spyro is a usual quick learner, able to master new abilities in a matter of hours. Due to this, he is convinced that he can be good at everything so he can put his new powers to good use to help defend Skylands. However Spyro isn't used to not being able to learn new abilities right away, feeling greatly disheartened when he isn't able to harness them despite being trained by Master Eon, the greatest among the Portal Masters. Although he is well in the company of his companions, Spyro possesses a headstrong and impulsive side. In The Machine of Doom, he believed that he could do everything by himself, implying that Spyro was used to doing heroics on his own prior to becoming a Skylander. This resulted in him struggling to work in a team at first (with his Skylander companions always reminding Spyro that he doesn't have to do everything by himself). However, his headstrong trait has presumably diminished during the course of being a Skylander when Spyro gradually became more humble, as shown in Spyro versus The Mega Monsters when he shared his victory over Kaos with the other Skylanders who helped him. He always keeps his temper in check, but there are times when he allows his emotions to get the better of him. After many adventures with the Skylanders, Spyro grew into a natural leader dedicated to scorching the forces of darkness. He takes his role as a Skylander seriously after being taught by Master Eon and holds deep insight regarding his fellow Skylanders, seeing them as more than just a team, but family, making them an unstoppable force against the toughest of foes. According to Roller Brawl, Spyro's leadership is on par with a roller derby's pivot, 'establishing the team's strategy and sets the pace of the pack'. In Skylanders: Imaginators, Spyro still displays a slight cocky behavior and occasionally cracks a joke or two, much to the dismay of certain Skylanders. According to him, he is awesome, but a Skylander who does pretty good in handling Doomlanders is pretty cool in his book.
spyro.gameplay: As a magical purple dragon, Spyro has the ability to harness the power of the other elements, though he prefers to master fire. He can also charge at his enemies with his horns and knock down obstacles, even lighting them ablaze with the element of fire. Being a dragon, Spyro has the ability to fly. When energies of darkness are nearby, Spyro can use their power to transform into his dark alter ego - Dark Spyro. In Skylanders: Battlecast, Spyro's abilities mostly stay the same, though with debuffing effects to some of them; however, he also gains the ability to brand enemies magically with the Sigil of the Dragon. His Special Ability is Dragon Breath, which attacks all enemies, and his signature Gear is the Ampli-fier, steel enhancements with engraved runes for his wings that power him and his allies up.

abilities.name: Dragon's Fire
abilities.description: Spyro breathes balls of flame from his mouth, incinerating enemies.

abilities.name: Charge
abilities.description: Spyro runs head down knocking over enemies with his horns.

abilities.name: Long Range Raze
abilities.description: Enhancing Spyro's lung capacity, this ability lets Spyro shoot Flameballs that travel much farther than before.

abilities.name: Spyro's Flight
abilities.description: Spyro takes to the skies. Well, off the ground at least! Fly over water and move at great speed.

abilities.name: Sprint Charge
abilities.description: Fitness counts. Spyro is able to charge for a longer distance with this upgrade.

abilities.name: Triple Flameballs
abilities.description: Shoot 3 Flameballs instead of one.

abilities.name: Spyro's Earth Pound
abilities.description: Perform a devastating dive-bomb head smash while flying, damaging enemies all around you.

abilities.name: Fireslam!
abilities.description: While flying, press Attack 2 to allow Spyro to shoot fireballs and perform a flaming slam.

abilities.name: Head Start!
abilities.description: Summon a magic worm ally at the end of your charge and send it after your enemies.

abilities.name: Fire Shield
abilities.description: This upgrade generates fire shields around Spyro when he uses his Flameball attack.

abilities.name: Exploding Fireblast
abilities.description: Spyro's central Flameball ignites into an explosive force that not only does more damage but hits multiple enemies.

abilities.name: The Daybringer Flame
abilities.description: Hold down your primary power button to build up this attack, which generates a flame so big and bright it is said to bring daylight to the sky.

abilities.name: Stun Charge
abilities.description: Enemies hit by Spyro's charge become temporarily stunned.

abilities.name: Comet Dash
abilities.description: A magic aura surrounds Spyro's horns imbuing them with extra power and damage that burns enemies in its path.

abilities.name: Ibex's Wrath Charge
abilities.description: Find Spyro's extra gear. With this upgrade, Spyro builds up speed and such a destructive force that it causes the very air around him to ignite into the magical form of fiery ibex horns.

trivia: Throughout the games, Spyro's design features differ in gameplay and media, such as his horns, spines, and claw color.
In the Ruins of Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure, the young Mabu Quigley will say 'Haven't I seen you somewhere before?' if you use Spyro to talk to him.
According to the novel The Machine of Doom, Spyro was first found by Master Eon in Summer Forest, a homeworld from Spyro 2: Ripto's Rage!.
Spyro has the most variants of any Skylander, including Series 1, Dark, Legendary, Series 2, Series 3, Series 3 Dark, Mini, and Eon's Elite.
He is the only Console Starter Pack Skylander in Spyro's Adventure not to wield a weapon.
Spyro was one of the original four Skylanders made for the game's first prototype, Spyro's Kingdom.
In Imaginators, he is voiced by Matthew Mercer, taking over from Josh Keaton.

star-strike.name: Star Strike
star-strike.description: Star Strike is a Magic core Skylander who first appeared in Skylanders: Swap Force. She is a mysterious alien from the distant cosmos who possesses the ability to harness cosmic energy and reflect projectiles with her magical fans.
star-strike.biography: Looking for a way to magically banish the Skylanders, Kaos poured through every dusty scroll and ancient tome he could find. Upon stumbling across a rare and extremely powerful spell, he began to recite its words. However, he sneezed midway through the incantation. As a result, instead of sending the Skylanders far away, Star Strike was plucked from her home in the distant cosmos and brought into Skylands. Surprised, Kaos thought he’d won a powerful new ally in the mysterious and reserved Star Strike. But she knew evil when she saw it and promptly unleashed her fierce magical powers on him. Word of her victory over Kaos spread quickly and she was soon asked by Master Eon to join the Skylanders.
star-strike.personality: You can't pull the wool over this bewitching alien's eyes. She's most likely to send evil into orbit with her star fall blast. She is also described as reserved and mysterious.
star-strike.gameplay: Star Strike's gameplay revolves around projectile reflection. Her primary attack summons a star that attacks enemies and then returns to her; by using her secondary spin attack at the right moment, she can reflect the star to increase its power and damage. She can also summon stars from the sky to rain down on her foes.

abilities.name: Star Gate
abilities.description: Press Attack 1 to summon a powerful star that will attack nearby enemies then return. Reflect the returning star with Attack 2 to power it up and do more damage.

abilities.name: Cosmic Twirl
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 to preform a magical spin, reflecting any projectiles nearby.

abilities.name: Starfall
abilities.description: Press Attack 3 to cause stars to fall and damage nearby enemies. Press Attack 2 to deflect the stars at enemies that are farther away.

abilities.name: Star-Filled Sky
abilities.description: Press Attack 3 to cause even more stars to fall and damage nearby enemies

abilities.name: Your Biggest Fan
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 to spin and reflect projectiles. Spin radius is now increased making it more likely to deflect projectiles and power up the star.

abilities.name: Star Power
abilities.description: Press Attack 1 rapidly to shoot star shards at enemies that do increased damage.

abilities.name: Shooting Stars
abilities.description: Press Attack 1 rapidly to shoot many sparkling star projectiles at nearby enemies.

abilities.name: Star Light
abilities.description: Starfall now causes a massive explosive star to fall from the sky. Press Attack 2 to deflect it at enemies.

abilities.name: Star Struck
abilities.description: Press Attack 3 to cause powerful stars that do increased damage to fall and damage nearby enemies.

abilities.name: Star Bright
abilities.description: Starfall can be used two times. Set up a star field blockade.

abilities.name: Atom Splitter
abilities.description: Press Attack 1 to shoot a star projectile. Press Attack 2 when it is close to deflect it and shoot two smaller projectiles.

abilities.name: Star Evasion
abilities.description: Armor is increased. No one would have thought that a dress could be so sturdy.

abilities.name: Super Star
abilities.description: Press Attack 1 to shoot a star projectile. Press Attack 2 when it is close to deflect it. Deflecting four times makes it grow larger and do more damage.

trivia: Star Strike is the one Skylander who can perform her secondary attack, the Cosmic Twirl, while jumping or after stepping on the bounce pad in Swap Force.
Star Strike was originally called Fan Girl.
Despite being the second female Magic Skylander while Ninjini was the first, Star Strike is the first female core Magic Skylander (second one being Déjà Vu).
Coincidentally, they all have featureless eyes.
When she shoots her star at the sheep, their wool changes colors. She is the second Magic Skylander to possess this ability, while Double Trouble was the first with his Eldritch Beam.
Star Strike was a character that people loved instantly, and when the developers showed them that she could reflect her own projectiles, players would just lose their minds.
She slightly resembles Raven from Teen Titans (but only when Raven has her hood on).

She also has similarities with Starfire from "Teen Titans" as both are female, aliens, protagonists, can fly (Star Strike hovers above the ground due to her not having visible legs.), have energy attacks and have the word "star" as the first syllable of their names.

She also resembles Architect from Battle Camp as both have color black in their hoods and outfits, color white and fan shape in their blades, and a shadowy face (Star Strike's face is shadowy except her eyes).
She and Blastermind are both alien based creatures of the Magic Element.
She has the Magic symbol on her tessons (when put together), her dress, and her cape button.

Both Star Strike's cape and hood seem to be held by her golden button, have the same color scheme, and don't match the rest of her outfit. This could mean that her cape and hood are the same piece of cloth.
Star Strike's voice actress, Misty Lee, is known as a professional magician.

Star Strike is noticeably similar to Spotlight: Their attacks are both linked with light, they both have featureless eyes, they are both voiced by Misty Lee, and they both share the same quote, "Time to Shine!"
As a LightCore figure, her eyes light up. Also, after she purchases her Soul Gem ability, "Shooting Star", her face almost lights up completely blocking her glowing eyes within the game.
She, Gearshift, and Rocky Roll are the only Skylanders that has the same number in all their stats.
Her and Enigma's faces are covered by their hoods. Coincidentally, they are both of the Magic element. However Star Strike's eyes can be seen, while Enigma's head is invisible.
Her quote "Starlight, star fight!" is the base for the pun of Lob-Star's official catchphrase "Star Bright, Star Fight!"

starcast.name: Starcast
starcast.description: Starcast is a black alien with four arms, each holding a star. He wears a gold helmet and the sensei gold belt. He is a Dark Sensei who trains Imaginators of the Ninja Battle Class.
starcast.biography: No one knows where Starcast came from, including Starcast himself! He was first seen falling out of the sky and landing directly on top of Master Eon, after he had made a wish for a Ninja Master to train the new generation of Skylanders. While it appeared that Eon's wish had come true, it was later revealed that Pop Fizz had simultaneously made a wish to get out of anger management lessons with the old Portal Master. Therefore, it was impossible to determine if Starcast was the result of one wish or the other. But after a brief martial arts display, it was clear to all that the mysterious Starcast was a very skilled ninja warrior. And seeing as how Master Eon had to walk around in crutches for the next few weeks, it was also clear that anger management class would have to be postponed – so it was a win-win!
starcast.personality: A mysterious and very skilled ninja warrior who fallen from the sky to train the next generation of Skylanders.
starcast.gameplay: Starcast uses his inter-dimensional powers for the Ninja Class. Having four arms he is able to rapid fire shurikens from the Dark Dimension, this is later upgraded when he fires two more powerful shurikens at the end of a combo and drop dangerous shards whilst jumping. Starcast is also able to conjure a rideable Megastar which mows down any enemy in his path but can still take damage whilst riding - on the Megastar, Starcast can throw larger and explosive shurikens. If he comes under enemy attention, he is able to disappear and attack whilst summoning a decoy which distracts and attacks enemies. The decoy later causes a vortex before it disappears, drawing enemies together. Depending on which path is chosen, Starcast can either upgrade the decoy or Megastar.

trivia: Starcast is one of the few multi-armed Skylanders, others being Slam Bam and Thrillipede.
His color scheme and appearance bear a resemblance to Legendary Slam Bam, though his figure is slightly translucent, as can be seen when held up to a light source.

Additionally, he bares strong resemblances to both Slam Bam and Star Strike. His body shape is very similar to the yeti, and he is also an extraterrestrial with featureless eyes much like her. Coincidentally, Starcast and Slam Bam are both voiced by Fred Tatasciore, and he and Star Strike do not originiate from Skylands.
Both Starcast and Flashwing were summoned or created by wishes, having no memories prior to them.
His color scheme resembles the night sky, the stars on his body even twinkle.
Both Starcast and Spotlight were summoned by Master Eon's will.
Starcast's battle quote 'Darkness there, and nothing more,' is a line from Edgar Allan Poe's famous poem 'The Raven.'
Both Ka-Boom and Starcast have outfits but are shirtless.
While on a rail in a grind challenge, he is seen running on it instead of actually sliding.
If Starcast uses his Interdimensional Shurikens while jumping, he will shoot down four shurikens and somersault when he hits the ground.

Like Stealth Elf, Starcast employs the decoy based ninjutsu art known as the Bushin No Justu, by deploying a decoy that distracts or fools enemies, allowing him to escape or otherwise confuse the enemy.

Starcast's shurikens are shaped just like the Hira Shaken, which were shuriken that commonly had a hole in them, and were of many different shapes. They were aerodynamic and easy to carry as they could be placed on one's belt. However, the manner in which Starcast deploys the shurikens are much more combat oriented and fictionalized rather then the much more tactical and defensive real life appliances.
One of his upgrades, 'Get over here!' is a reference to a quote from Scorpion, a character from the Mortal Kombat franchise.

Starcast bears multiple similarities to Hidden Phantom, one of the Four Guardians in the Mega Man Zero series. Both of them are ninja with dark or shadow elementality, both use shuriken in combat and even ride a bigger one, and use clones in combat to distract enemies.
Starcast, Spyro, Dino-Rang, Star Strike, Enigma, Hammer Slam Bowser, Turbo Charge Donkey Kong, Crash Bandicoot, and Dr. Neo Cortex are the only Skylanders who do not originate from Skylands.
Starcast's appearance resembles that of the Celestialsapien alien species from the Ben 10 series.
His Chase Variants, Clear Starcast and Happy Birthday Ben Starcast, are the only dark elemental chase variants.

stealth-elf.name: Stealth Elf
stealth-elf.description: Stealth Elf is an elven ninja who is one of the playable Skylanders in the Skylanders series. Her Legendary counterpart is Legendary Stealth Elf, who is a Toys R Us exclusive. She has a Series 3 counterpart called Ninja Stealth Elf, and she is also one of the three starter Skylanders in Skylanders: Ring of Heroes.
stealth-elf.biography: As a small child, Stealth Elf awoke one morning inside the hollow of an old tree with no memory of how she got there. She was taken in by an unusually stealthy, ninja-like forest creature in the deep forest. Under his tutelage, she has spent the majority of her life training in the art of stealth fighting. After completing her training, she became a Skylander and set out into the world to uncover the mystery behind her origins.
stealth-elf.personality: Stealth Elf, like all elves, adores nature. She is considered to be a guardian protector of the forests and of Skylands. She may be a highly trained ninja, but sometimes Stealth Elf is known to have a sense of a rampaging Cyclops Mammoth. She speaks her mind, whether others want to hear it or not. She can sneak her way into any enemy's territory, but can also be tactless. Like all Life Skylanders, Stealth Elf prefers to keep her feet on the ground. Stealth Elf is also known to use trickery to get out of situations she doesn't feel like doing herself, using her decoys. She also appears to be tomboyish as well.
stealth-elf.gameplay: Being quite swift and agile, Stealth Elf able to skewer and slash swiftly at her enemies with her daggers. She can also create scarecrows of herself that wield scythes to attack other foes and can bring forth a copy of herself as a decoy to distract other enemies while she turns invisible. She can even regenerate her lost health back overtime. Her series 2 wow pow allows her to spin in a blender style with her blades, while her series 3 wow pow allows her to summon a sabertooth tiger for a short time before dealing a powerful kick to enemies.

trivia: In her Series 1 and Series 2 toy form, her daggers and eyes glow in the dark.
She, Chill, Deja Vu, and Roller Brawl are currently the only female Skylanders with a Legendary counterpart.
Her original catchphrase was 'Now You See Me. Now You Don't'. But it eventually became, 'Silent, But Deadly!'.
It is implied that Stealth Elf had trained under numerous masters, including King Pen, Grandmaster Cami Flage, and her original master, Forester.
She is the only Life Skylander to be in a starter pack five times.
Her battle cry, 'Knock knock... too late!' would later be used as the catchphrase for Fist Bump.
She and Spyro are the only Skylanders to both have Dark, Legendary and Elite versions of themselves.
In her prototype toy model, Stealth Elf originally had red eyes.
In early 2025, Stealth Elf was the first character revealed for a collaboration between Skylanders and collectibles brand YouTooz.

steel-plated-hood-sickle.name: Steel Plated Hood Sickle
steel-plated-hood-sickle.description: Steel Plated Hood Sickle is a steel plated counterpart of Hood Sickle in Skylanders: Imaginators.
steel-plated-hood-sickle.biography: Steel Plated Hood Sickle is a steel plated counterpart of Hood Sickle in Skylanders: Imaginators.
steel-plated-hood-sickle.personality: Not much is known about Steel Plated Hood Sickle's personality, other than being a steel plated counterpart of Hood Sickle.
steel-plated-hood-sickle.gameplay: Steel Plated Hood Sickle is a Dark Sentinel Sensei in Skylanders: Imaginators. He shares the same moveset as Hood Sickle but features a unique steel-plated appearance. As a Sentinel, he uses his scythe to control the battlefield and teleport through darkness.

He's the only Alt Deco Skylander of the Dark element to have a toy.
His English voice actor is J.B. Blanc.

steel-plated-smash-hit.name: Steel Plated Smash Hit
steel-plated-smash-hit.description: Steel Plated Smash Hit is an alter ego of the Earth SuperCharger, Smash Hit in Skylanders: SuperChargers.
steel-plated-smash-hit.biography: It is widely known that few Skylanders enjoy demolition more that Smash Hit. But after finishing runner-up to Crusher in last year's annual Destruct-o-Thon, Smash Hit decided to enter this year's competition better prepared. Now reinforced with indestructible Skytanium steel, the young Warsupial is primed and ready to smash anything and everything the competition can throw his way!
steel-plated-smash-hit.personality: Smash Hit is a determined competitor who loves demolition and takes pride in being prepared for any challenge.
steel-plated-smash-hit.gameplay: Steel Plated Smash Hit's attacks include Demolisher, Crushinator, Connect and Disconnect, Heap, and G'Day. He focuses on high-impact demolition and flail-based combat.

trivia: Few Skylanders enjoy demolition more that Smash Hit.
Smash Hit finished runner-up to Crusher in an annual Destruct-o-Thon.
He is reinforced with indestructible Skytanium steel.

stink-bomb.name: Stink Bomb
stink-bomb.description: Being a skunk, Stink Bomb can really 'light the fuse' on his enemies, releasing a cloud of smelly vapor which damages enemies and renders him invisible. He can also throw ninja stars and perform a devastating One-Inch Palm which knocks back and poisons his foes. With certain upgrades, he can also launch nauseous acorns at enemies. Nauseated enemies turn green and take damage over a short period of time.
stink-bomb.biography: Stink Bomb studied martial arts under one of the greatest ninja masters in history, who believed that surprise was the key to finding your true self. Thus, his master would constantly jump out and frighten him, hoping that it would scare Stink Bomb into finding his innermost strength. On one such occasion, Stink Bomb was so surprised that he instinctively released a cloud of vapor so pungent that it caused his master to disappear and never return. With this newly discovered ability, Stink Bomb developed his own form of martial arts known as Kung Fume, and wandered the land teaching it to all those who wished to learn. It was not long before the news (and smell) of this new form reached Master Eon, who sought out the young ninja at once.
stink-bomb.personality: Resilient Stink Bomb didn't let his master's disappearance put him down. He developed the martial art Kung Fume and wandered Skylands teaching its whiffy ways. Like all Life Skylanders, Stink Bomb prefers to keep his feet on the ground.
stink-bomb.gameplay: Being a skunk, Stink Bomb can really 'light the fuse' on his enemies, releasing a cloud of smelly vapor which damages enemies and renders him invisible. He can also throw ninja stars and perform a devastating One-Inch Palm which knocks back and poisons his foes. With certain upgrades, he can also launch nauseous acorns at enemies. Nauseated enemies turn green and take damage over a short period of time. In Skylanders: Ring of Heroes, he functions as a debuff specialist using poison and accuracy-reducing effects.

trivia: Stink Bomb is similar to Stealth Elf, notably due to both Skylanders being ninjas, turn invisible and possess similar clothing.
He's also the second ninja Skylander (first being Stealth Elf, third being Lob-Star).

Whenever his top half is placed on the Portal of Power, a classic ninja theme with an ancient Japanese flute can be heard playing in the background, (which sounds similar to the flute theme being played in Ultrabeat's 2003 hit 'Pretty Green Eyes') along with a gong crashing at the end. When his bottom half is placed on the portal, it sprays a visible stinky smell from the tail's end.
Developer Rob Gallerani comments, 'I love Stink Bomb for the sheer number of meetings we had to have about the sound of his fart attack.'

His voice actor, Tom Kenny, is best known for portraying SpongeBob SquarePants, The Ice King from Adventure Time, Doctor Ocotpus in Ultimate Spider-Man, and is also the current voice of Spyro in his main video game series - first performing the role in Spyro 2: Ripto's Rage.
He and Night Shift are seen in most of the commercials of Swap Force, including the intro of the game. They're always seen swapping with each other.
Tom Kenny also voices Arbo and Shield Shredder, who are also Life-elemental creatures.
He and Trap Shadow are the only Sneak SWAP Force Skylanders. However, Stink Bomb can stay invisible longer than Trap Shadow even after pressing the second attack button once.
Everytime Stink Bomb disappears while wearing a hat, his headwear vanishes as well.
Unlike real skunks, his stinky smell is portrayed as farting.
Whenever his bottom half gets upgraded, the color of his belt changes, which is a reference to the martial arts ranking.
His One-Inch Palm ability is a pun of Bruce Lee's One-Inch Punch.
While battling Evil Glumshanks, the boss is unable to locate Stink Bomb while he is invisible. However, Evilized Whiskers is able to locate Stink Bomb even if he is unseen.

When collected, his Soul Gem states that his top half's ability is Tri-Star Technique which allows him to throw three stars at a time. In actuality, his Soul Gem ability only makes his stars have a higher critical hit ratio.
In Trap Team, 'Sporting Stripes' now makes any Swap Force Skylander using Stink Bomb's lower half move faster.
His only appearance in Skylanders: Battlecast is in one of Wash Buckler's cards called 'Stink or Swim.'

stormblade.name: Stormblade
stormblade.description: With speed as her friend, Stormblade can dash about the battlefield hurling feathered blades and strike enemies like a moving torpedo.
stormblade.biography: From the moment she left the nest, Stormblade had always pushed the boundaries, seeking to travel further than anyone had ever gone. At a young age, she made the bold leap off of her home island and plummeted through the deep blue sky in an attempt to find the bottom of Skylands – only to find no such bottom existed. This did not fulfill her curiosity, nor did it sway her belief there was something else beyond the limits of her world. Soon she built a custom ship, the Sky Slicer, and raced to the furthest reaches of Skylands in search of its end – but no end could be found. She wanted answers, and so she came to the one person that could help her – Master Eon. The Portal Master instantly saw the unquenchable thirst for exploration that resided in Stormblade, and asked her to join the Skylanders on a very special mission that would take her through the uncharted rifts between worlds!
stormblade.personality: Stormblade is a fearless daredevil with an unquenchable thirst for adventure. She is naturally excited about things, including participating in missions and dedicating herself to training. Stormblade is also very confident in the good in people she looks up to, as seen in her attempts to redeem Ghost Roaster in Secret Agent Secrets. However, her tendency to not stick to one thought also makes her somewhat slow on the uptake, as seen on Story of Nightfall where she mistakes Nightfall's story about traumatized citizens to be about mind attacks from Leviathans.
stormblade.gameplay: In Skylanders: Battlecast, she can also summon the Sky Slicer for a Strafing Run, assume the Lightning Claw Stance to gain power and intimidate her enemies, and shoot blade beams randomly. Her Special Ability are the Feather Blades to randomly attack an enemy, and her signature gear is the Beam Splitter, a cubic prism that adds damage to previous attacks. Stormblade is also notable in that, like Jet-Vac, her special abilities are cheap to use and very powerful if the random numbers favor the player. Her scrapped signature relic is the Slicer Beacon, which can call upon the Sky Slicer when they obtain cards.

trivia: Stormblade is the first female Air Skylander who is bipedal.
Stormblade is one of only two Skylanders to soften their landing when falling, with the other Skylander being Dune Bug.
Her ability to shoot feathered blades from her wings is similar to Falcon from Marvel.
She is the third Skylander to have the word 'blade' in her name, after Freeze Blade and Blades.
Stormblade's voice actress, Stephanie Lemelin, is known for voicing Artemis Crock, Green Arrow's niece and sidekick, in Young Justice.
One of her upgrades is named exactly the same as her catchphrase, namely 'Feather the Storm.'

stump-smash.name: Stump Smash
appearances: Stump Smash Crosses the Bone Dragon
stump-smash.description: Stump Smash is an ent who is one of the main core Skylanders in Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure. He is of the Life element.
stump-smash.biography: Stump Smash was once a magical tree that spent most of his time sleeping peacefully in the forests of Skylands. Then one day he awoke to discover his entire forest had been chopped down and logged by trolls– himself included. His long branches were gone, leaving him with only powerful mallets for hands, which he used to smash the troll tree-cutting machines. Although still grumpy about what happened to him, Stump Smash has vowed to protect Skylands against those who would do it harm… especially trolls.
stump-smash.personality: Prior to being cut down and logged, Stump Smash was a peaceful tree creature who spent most of his lifetime sleeping in the forest areas of his world, that is, until his incident with the Trolls. To this day, Stump Smash is still grouchy about what happened to him and takes his anger out on evil doers. He knows how to bare a grudge. Even after all these years he still seeks out trolls to teach them a lesson. He's no sap.[3]
stump-smash.gameplay:
Despite having his branches chopped, Stump Smash can still attack his enemies by slamming them with his mallet-like hands. He also has the ability to spit and roll a large, spiked acorn upon his opponents, and can spit out smaller acorns at his opponent that will cause branches to grow on the enemy's body, slowing them down as a result. He can even regain health when in water. In 'Stump Smash crosses the Bone Dragon' it's shown that he can use his own life force energy to speed the growth of plants, as he used it on the acorns he spit out, which caused them to grow into large trees that tangled the Bone Dragon.

On the Smash 'N' Bash path, Stump Smash gains extra abilities with the Meganut and combos. He can now rapidly charge forward and attack enemies around him with the Stump Crusher Combos upgrade, giving him multiple ways to deal with enemies in melee range. The Acorn Croquet upgrade allows him to send the Meganut flying towards enemies, further increasing the Meganut's potential range, allowing it to strike enemies from very far away. Finally, the Smash Meganut upgrade allows Stump Smash to make the Meganut explode, dealing massive damage to enemies around the nut, and since the nut starts close to Stump Smash, it can be used to deal heavy damage to enemies up close. Overall, this path further improves Stump Smash's melee capabilities and ability to deal with single opponents, giving him a more up-close and personal fighting style, though retaining some amount of ranged ability.

On the Nut Crafter upgrade path, Stump Smash gains extra abilities with his acorns. The first upgrade, Pollen Plume, improves his abilities to deal damage to clusters of enemies, allowing him to slow down multiple enemies with a single acorn. The second upgrade, Meganut Propagation, lets Stump Smash turn the Meganut into a group of acorns that spread out, and thus deal with enemies that surround him at a distance. The final upgrade, Double Nut, allows Stump Smash to fire two acorns at once, rolling across the ground to slow down more enemies at a time. Overall, this path increases Stump Smash's ability to deal with crowds of enemies, debilitating them with the ability to send several acorns in multiple methods and slow down multiple enemies at time, making them easy pickings for his melee damage.
