trivia: Stump Smash was originally brown during gameplay prior to his character trailer.
He is the first non-earth Skylander that uses hammers as weapons (the second being Hammer Slam Bowser).
His promo title 'Tree Rex' is shared by the Giant Skylander of the same name.
When floating in the water (possible with the Soul Gem ability), press the Attack Button to squirt water out of Stump Smash's mouth.[6]
In the boss battle with the Evil Ent, he charges up his Meganuts and Acorns before launching them, while the real Stump Smash is incapable of doing so.
Stump Smash, Lightning Rod and Double Trouble are the only non-Water Skylanders that can cross over water without the ability to fly.
He has the highest amount of health out of all of the Core Skylanders.
The original name for the Smash-N-Bash path is the Nut Master path.
Stump Smash is the only Skylander who has their magic moment changed in Giants.
He and Tree Rex are both Skylanders who resemble trees and are voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson.
Because Swap Force has excluded the ability to swim, Stump Smash, Zap and Double Trouble's soul gems have changed.
In Skylanders: Lost Islands, Stump Smash mentions having feelings for Frilly, and has gone on a date with her at least once with the help of the Portal Master.
Stump Smash was one of the many Skylanders planned to appear in Skylanders: Ring of Heroes. Before the game's closure, only concept art of his Awakened Form was released.
If Stump Smash has his Thornbark upgrade and falls during a Ring Out Battle Arena, he fires thorns as his plummets out of the arena.
His Japanese dub voice actor, Soichi Abe, also portrayed Eruptor in the Japanese dub of Skylanders Academy.

sun-dragon.name: Sun Dragon
sun-dragon.description: Sun Dragon is a scrapped character and the original design of Camo. He only appeared briefly in the Skylanders: The Beginning trailer, taking part in the battle against Kaos' army.
sun-dragon.biography: Sun Dragon was one of the earliest Skylanders designed, present during the initial pitch of a Toy-themed Spyro game as a playable dragon, and as a Life Skylander during the Spyro's Kingdom phase. At this point, Sun Dragon had a more menacing design with a larger head. Despite being present in early trailers, the Sun Dragon design was eventually replaced with Camo's current design seemingly late in development. The two have an identical moveset.
sun-dragon.personality: Sun Dragon was designed with a more intimidating and menacing appearance compared to the final version of Camo. While he was never given a spoken personality in the final games, his early concept art suggests a fiercer, more primal nature.
sun-dragon.gameplay: Sun Dragon's gameplay was centered around life-based magic and explosive pyrotechnics. Like Camo, he would have summoned firecracker vines to trap enemies and fired sun bursts to deal ranged damage.

abilities.name: Sun Burst
abilities.description: Fires a concentrated burst of sun energy at enemies.

abilities.name: Firecracker Vines
abilities.description: Summons vines that explode upon contact with enemies.

trivia: Interestingly, he, Fire Kraken and Flare Wolf are the only Skylanders who used fireworks to fight. However because Sun Dragon was scrapped, Fire Kraken and Flare Wolf are the only ones.
Coincidentally, both Fire Kraken and Sun Dragon are chinese dragons.
Although Sun Dragon is a scrapped version of Camo, Camo also appears independently in The Beginning trailer, charging into battle just under Spyro's wing.
The Sun Dragon can only ever be seen twice in 'The Beginning' trailer.
The first time is when Slam Bam is fighting some Cyclops Choppers. Sun Dragon can be seen in the background to the left of Slam Bam.
The second and final time is when the Skylanders are being blasted away. He can again be seen in the background, this time to the left of Wrecking Ball as the grub worm says 'Not good.'
The dragon heads on the door archways around the Creepy Citadel are modelled after Sun Dragon. The dragon torches around the Quicksilver Vault are also modeled after him.
Sun Dragon bears a slight resemblance to Shenron of the Dragon Ball franchise.
He is seen in the first cutscene of Skylanders: SuperChargers, in the flashback with footage from The Beginning trailer when Kaos talks about the Skylanders defeating him for years.

sunburn.name: Sunburn
sunburn.description: Sunburn is a Fire phoenix/dragon hybrid Skylander in Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure. He is bundled with the Dragon's Peak Adventure Pack.
sunburn.biography: Born in the center of an active volcano, Sunburn is part dragon, part phoenix, and 100% fire power. He is very proud of his unique heritage, and is the only dragon and phoenix hybrid known to exist in Skylands. This rare combination makes him a desirable target for dark wizards and bounty hunters that seek to gain power by unlocking the secrets behind Sunburn’s ability to teleport. Joining the Skylanders gave Sunburn a way to help defend the world from evil, but also provided him with protection, as he remains one of the most sought after creatures in Skylands.
sunburn.personality: Like all dragons, Sunburn is quite the prankster, but hates evil with a passion. He uses his powers of teleportation to play practical jokes on his Skylander buddies, appearing when they least expect it. He doesn't like to stay in one place for more than a minute at a time.
sunburn.gameplay: Sunburn has the ability to breathe streams of fire. He also has a unique ability to teleport from one place to another, leaving a trail of flames behind. Sunburn is able to perform a fiery dash, where his speed increases while burning enemies in his path, which ends in an fiery explosion. It is said that his body temperature is so hot that his very molecules can't remain in one place and will teleport to a new location. Truth to be told, this ability has nothing to do with temperature, but is in fact a side effect of Sunburn being the only known half-dragon half-phoenix to exist.

abilities.name: Flamethrower Breath
abilities.description: Unleash a stream of flame breath

abilities.name: Immolation Teleport
abilities.description: Teleport to another location, leaving a damaging flame behind.

abilities.name: Guided Teleportation
abilities.description: Control the direction of your teleport.

abilities.name: Blazethrower
abilities.description: Flamethrower Breath does increased damage.

abilities.name: Phoenix Dash
abilities.description: Perform a Phoenix Dash.

abilities.name: Immolation Inflammation
abilities.description: Flames left behind after teleporting do increased damage.

abilities.name: Flight of the Phoenix
abilities.description: Phoenix Dash lasts longer, does more damage, and ends with a blast.

abilities.name: Infinite Flame
abilities.description: Endlessly use the Flamethrower Breath attack.

abilities.name: Intense Heat
abilities.description: Hold the Flamethrower Breath attack longer for extra damage.

abilities.name: Phoenix Grand Blaze
abilities.description: Hold Flamethrower Breath long enough to be surrounded by flame and do extra damage.

abilities.name: Immolation Destruction
abilities.description: Flames left behind after teleporting are larger and do extra damage.

abilities.name: Flame Streaks
abilities.description: Teleporting creates streaks of flames that damage enemies.

abilities.name: Burning Trail
abilities.description: Streaks of flames do increased damage.

trivia: Images of Hot Flash, Sunburn's earlier reptilian design, can be found in early coloring book images and on the Skylanders Spyro's Adventure Carrying Case product.
This original artwork is mistakenly displayed in Battle Mode of Spyro's Adventure (possibly a glitch exclusive to specific versions).

Sunburn, along with Flashwing, Scratch and Blades are the only four winged Skylanders who cannot fly in game; however, Sunburn and Flashwing are both seen flying in their promotion trailers, and both Sunburn and Scratch hover while performing some attacks (in Sunburn's case, he slightly hovers when using his Phoenix Dash attack).
However, he is able to fly or at least hover in the 3DS version of Spyro's Adventure and Giants.
Sunburn's feathers are so hot, you can fry a troll egg on them!

He is one of the Skylanders in Spyro's Adventure who didn't make it to being a Series 2 in Skylanders: Giants (the others being Boomer, Camo, Voodood, Ghost Roaster, Warnado, Dino-Rang, and Wham-Shell) although Wham-Shell and Warnado get LightCore versions of themselves in Swap Force, Camo gets a Series 2 in the game and the rest of those Skylanders (Except for Sunburn) have an Eon's Elite in SuperChargers).
While he doesn't make a Series 2 counterpart, his evil counterpart, the Evil Phoenix Dragon, appears in the chapter of the former mentioned game, Glacier Gully as an ambush in the Elemental Gate.
As of Imaginators, Sunburn is the only dragon from Spyro's Adventure who never got a Series 2 or LightCore counterpart.
He is able to teleport, and uses this ability to play pranks on the other Skylanders.
He shares some similarities to Skywarp from the Transformers franchise: Both are teleporting pranksters capable of flight.
In the Skylanders Giants Official Guide, at one point, he is mistakenly called Sunbeam.
At another part, he is referred to as female.
The explosions his teleporting ability leaves behind have a much smaller area of effect after Giants compared to the first game.
He is also the only Skylander to have an area named after them, as in Dragon's Peak there is an area called Sunburn's Rest.
However, a non-Skylander has a place named after it as well - Quigley (Quigley's Grotto).

Sunburn is voiced by Troy Baker, who also voices Steeljaw in Transformers: Robots in Disguise (2015), Joel from The Last of Us, Loki in multiple Marvel Animated series, and Batman in Lego Batman 2: DC Superheroes.
He and Blades are currently the only two dragon Skylanders who came in Adventure Packs.
Sunburn is the only Skylander from Spyro's Adventure who has not had a repose in any sequel game so far.

sundae-slobber-tooth.name: Sundae Slobber Tooth
sundae-slobber-tooth.description: 'Sundae Slobber Tooth has come to celebrate savory summer sundaes in Skylands!'
sundae-slobber-tooth.biography: 'Sundae Slobber Tooth is an ice cream counterpart of Slobber Tooth in Skylanders: Lost Islands, introduced in July 2014 as an Alter Ego variant to celebrate the summer season.'
sundae-slobber-tooth.personality: 'Sundae Slobber Tooth is a festive and sweet-toothed version of the original Slobber Tooth, known for his persistence and love for frozen treats.'
sundae-slobber-tooth.gameplay: 'As an Alter Ego in Skylanders: Lost Islands, Sundae Slobber Tooth provides players with a unique visual variant of Slobber Tooth that maintains the base character's mechanics and utility within the game.'
trivia: He is an Alter Ego variant specifically released for the mobile game Skylanders: Lost Islands.
His design is themed after an ice cream sundae, including scoops on his back and a cherry on his head.
He was released in July 2014.

super-shot-stealth-elf.name: Super Shot Stealth Elf
super-shot-stealth-elf.description: Super Shot Stealth Elf is the SuperChargers counterpart of Stealth Elf in Skylanders: SuperChargers. Her signature vehicle is the Stealth Stinger.
super-shot-stealth-elf.biography: Super Shot Stealth Elf is the SuperChargers counterpart of Stealth Elf in Skylanders: SuperChargers. Her signature vehicle is the Stealth Stinger. Separated from her parents at a young age, Stealth Elf was raised by a mysterious forest ninja who trained her in the art of stealth. As a SuperCharger, she has upgraded her arsenal with a high-tech Dagger Cannon to take on the Darkness and protect Skylands.
super-shot-stealth-elf.personality: Stealth Elf is a disciplined, mysterious, and highly focused ninja. She is a dedicated protector of Skylands who values speed and precision, often letting her actions speak louder than her words.
super-shot-stealth-elf.gameplay: In Skylanders: SuperChargers Racing, Super Shot Stealth Elf is mostly all-around in her stats. She has balanced Top Speed and Acceleration, as well as Firepower and Armour. Her best stat is her Handling, which is set to the maximum value for a driver. As a SuperCharger, she has access to the vehicle mods. As an AI racer, she uses the Tomb Buggy with the Ghastly Speedster mods for Land races, the Splatter Splasher with the Acrylic Spoiler mods for Sea races, and her Stealth Stinger with the SuperCharged mods for Sky races.

abilities.name: Dagger Cannon
abilities.description: Press Attack 1 and hold to lock onto enemies and shoot daggers at them. Yes, it's a gun that shoots daggers.

abilities.name: Say Hello
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 to disappear and create a turret that distracts enemies.

abilities.name: Circle Slash
abilities.description: Press Attack 3 to perform an acrobatic spin that hits and knocks back enemies nearby.

abilities.name: Needle-pointed Daggers
abilities.description: Dagger Cannon deals more damage. Straight to the point!

abilities.name: To My Little Friend
abilities.description: The turret now shoots enemies in front of it.

abilities.name: Speed of the Spin
abilities.description: Gain increased movement speed for a short time after using Circle Slash.

abilities.name: Health Elf
abilities.description: After injury and after defeating an enemy, a familiar face appears and brings a health bonus!

abilities.name: Smog Slash
abilities.description: Create a poison cloud when you exit stealth mode.

abilities.name: All Wound Up
abilities.description: Dagger Cannon projectiles do more damage the longer Attack 1 is held.

abilities.name: Splinter Shells
abilities.description: Dagger Cannon projectiles splinter off enemies and hit nearby enemies.

abilities.name: Distraction Destruction
abilities.description: On expiration, the turret explodes and damages nearby enemies.

abilities.name: Acquisition Intelligence Mode
abilities.description: The turret now aims at nearby enemies and does more damage.

abilities.name: Spin to Win!
abilities.description: Circle Slash does more damage and knocks enemies further away.

trivia: Her Soul Gem power summons her Mini counterpart, Whisper Elf.
Super Shot Stealth Elf has dramatic changes in her gameplay from to her regular counterpart, changing from melee and crowd control tactics to a mostly ranged moveset.
She has even less health than her regular counterpart, being less than even Trigger Happy and Spitfire.
One of her upgrades shares the name of Wind-Up's catchphrase.
The upgrades 'Say hello' and 'to my little friend' when combined are a reference to a quote from the film Scarface.
When she, Big Bubble Pop Fizz, Deep Dive Gill Grunt and Bone Bash Roller Brawl are placed on the portal, they say their official catchphrases in a slightly different tone of their voices.
She, regular Stealth Elf and the Golden Queen are the only female Skylanders with dark edition counterparts.
She and Shark Shooter Terrafin are the only SuperCharger versions of previous Skylanders in Skylanders: Ring of Heroes.
She was originally going to be additionally released in a single pack, but was unreleased for unknown reasons.
Her Needle-pointed daggers upgrade includes a description identical to Pop Thorn's catchphrase: 'Straight to the point!'

Super Shot Stealth Elf underwent a number of drastically different iterations in development. Concept art depicts her with a mohawk and arm fan, various alternate masks, and bizarre weaponry such as a giant hoop, a rocket mounted on her back, a horse-headed stick, and a propeller cap.

superchargers.name: SuperChargers
superchargers.description: Master Eon assembled this special team of heroes to pilot the Rift Engine-powered vehicles and stop Kaos from using the Sky Eater to consume the world. The team consists of both new recruits and legendary veterans whose powers were enhanced by the Rift Engines.
superchargers.biography: The SuperChargers are a group of Skylanders in Skylanders: SuperChargers that are trained to pilot the most powerful Vehicles in Skylands, using the power of the Rift Engines to enhance their own powers and their Vehicles'. When a SuperCharger hops into their signature Vehicle, it becomes SuperCharged, gaining a new appearance, a damage boost and other perks. Certain SuperChargers are previous Skylanders that, upon coming into contact with Rift Engines, were given new appearances and abilities.
superchargers.personality: The SuperChargers are a courageous and mechanically gifted group of heroes. Comprising both legendary veterans and new recruits, they are characterized by their determination to master the terrains of land, sea, and sky to protect the Skylands.
superchargers.gameplay: In Skylanders: SuperChargers, these characters are unique for their ability to pilot vehicles. When a SuperCharger is paired with their specific signature vehicle, the vehicle becomes 'SuperCharged,' which alters its appearance, boosts its stats, and provides a unique weapon upgrade. This allows for diverse combat strategies across Land, Sea, and Sky zones.

abilities.name: Pilot Vehicles
abilities.description: SuperChargers are uniquely trained to pilot the most powerful Vehicles in Skylands using the power of the Rift Engines.

abilities.name: Rift Engine Enhancement
abilities.description: Using the power of Rift Engines, SuperChargers can enhance their own inherent powers as well as those of their Vehicles.

abilities.name: SuperCharged
abilities.description: When a SuperCharger hops into their signature Vehicle, it becomes SuperCharged, gaining a new appearance, a damage boost, and other perks.

trivia: In the game cutscene featuring the SuperChargers, their signature vehicles don't change into their SuperCharged forms despite being driven by their respective riders.

The SuperChargers are illustrated in the books about The Darkness in the Spell Punk Library as the Skylanders that fought the evil centuries ago, despite the illustrations taking place in a far earlier time period.
The SuperChargers are the first team of Skylanders to consist of returning Skylanders from previous titles.
None of the reposed SuperChargers originated from Skylanders: Trap Team.
All of the reposed SuperChargers are completely incompatible with previous games.
Except for Bone Bash Roller Brawl, all the reposed SuperChargers have had at least one Wow Pow reposed figure in the previous games.
Turbo Charge Donkey Kong and Hammer Slam Bowser are the only SuperChargers whose elements don't match with their respective Vehicles.
In addition, they're the only ones with words that don't have matching first letters in their name unlike the returning Skylanders as SuperChargers, not counting variants.

The new characters introduced as Superchargers are all Skylanders recruited after the events of Skylanders: Trap Team, including as a direct result of events that happened in previous games. They are also part of the first namesake group to have been recruited after the events of Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure.
In very early concepts of SuperChargers and their vehicles, Magna Charge, Free Ranger and Spyro were possible candidates before the vehicle types were decided on.
With exception of Thrillipede, the guest characters and almost all the reposed Skylanders, all the SuperChargers were playable in Skylanders: Ring of Heroes.
Earth is the only Element where all of its SuperChargers were playable in Ring of Heroes.

surfer-slam-bam.name: Surfer Slam Bam
surfer-slam-bam.description: Surfer Slam Bam has ridden a huge wave into the Kingdom.
surfer-slam-bam.biography: Surfer Slam Bam is the Summer counterpart of Slam Bam. He was available exclusively on Skylanders: Lost Islands during the month of June 2013.
surfer-slam-bam.catchphrase: Surfer Slam Bam has ridden a huge wave into the Kingdom.
surfer-slam-bam.personality: Not much is known about Surfer Slam Bam's personality, other than his association with summer and surfing themes.
surfer-slam-bam.gameplay: Surfer Slam Bam was available exclusively on Skylanders: Lost Islands during the month of June 2013. As an Alter Ego, he is a non-playable character in the main console games and does not possess a traditional move set.
trivia: Surfer Slam Bam is the first summer themed variant.
He is the first non-Legendary variant of a Water elemental Skylander.
He is the first Alter Ego to have exclusive character artwork.

swap-force.name: SWAP Force
swap-force.description: The SWAP Force, also known as the SWAP Force Skylanders, are a special group of Skylanders who have the ability to mix and match their abilities and powers. They made their debut in Skylanders: Swap Force.
swap-force.biography: During an epic battle, a brave group of Skylanders were caught in the eruption of a mystical volcano in the Cloudbreak Islands while defending the Ancient Elementals from servants of the Darkness. The result blasted them apart and sent them to Earth. But the magic of the volcano gave these heroes a remarkable new power -- the ability to swap halves with each other -- turning them into a special team known as the SWAP Force.
swap-force.personality: A team of brave, versatile heroes known for their cooperation and ability to adapt to any combat situation by sharing their unique strengths.
swap-force.gameplay: SWAP Force characters can be physically separated into two pieces (the top half and the bottom half). Players can combine the top half of one Skylander with the bottom half of another to create a custom hybrid with unique attacks and movement types. This mechanic allows for 256 unique combinations, each with distinct elemental powers and movement types like Rocket, Spin, Speed, and Sneak.

abilities.name: Swapabilities
abilities.description: The magic of the Cloudbreak volcano allows these heroes to swap halves, mixing and matching their attacks and movement types.

abilities.name: Swappable, Unstoppable!
abilities.description: The ability to physically separate and combine with any other member of the team, creating 256 unique hybrid combinations.

trivia: This team was originally named the ShapeShifters.
This is the only special team of Skylanders to be entirely male. This is due to Vicarious Visions wanting to take a 'gender neutral approach' to the SWAP Force so the swapping would make sense.

Only seven of the SWAP Force Skylanders appeared in the console storyline of Skylanders: Swap Force. However, in the Nintendo 3DS version's introduction, they switched out Freeze Blade with Rattle Shake.
Wash Buckler is the only member of the SWAP Force to appear in Skylanders: Battlecast.

In the Switch version of Skylanders: Imaginators, when you scan in a SWAP Force character, they will have none of their upgrades, but they will be at level 20, and they will have no gold. This is due to the Joy-Con only being able to scan the bottom half of the SWAP Force figures.
Additionally, they're the only Skylanders in the Switch version of Skylanders: Imaginators that cannot be deleted.
Originally, the SWAP Force were going to have the ability to swap heads.

There were also several SWAP Force Skylanders that didn't make it into the final game, used for the game's initial pitch and kid testing. One of them was Krayken (who later became the core Skylander, Rip Tide), a dinosaur named Aftershock, and Breezewing. They were all eventually scrapped as they did not fit the design philosophy of the series, had negative feedback during the first test, and were far too large.

However, Krayken and Breezewing do make a cameo in the Enchanted Elven Forest as swimming floats. Oddly, Breezewing has also been also seen in Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure development art, indicating she was passed around both developers.
Interestingly enough, Aftershock would be a placeholder name for the Skylander, Fist Bump.

The name of Spy Rise's top half 'Spy' is the shortest of all the SWAP Force's top halves, while the name of Boom Jet's bottom half 'Jet' is the shortest of all the SWAP Force's bottom halves, each only have three letters.
There are a total of 256 combinations.

swarm.name: Swarm
swarm.description: Swarm is a giant hornet-like hymenopteran insect who is one of the eight Giants in Skylanders: Giants. He is of the Air element.
swarm.biography: Swarm was once a prince from a proud race of mysterious insect warriors that had built their entire civilization inside a giant honeycombed pyramid. Growing up as one of the 9,000 members of the royal family, he was never permitted to leave the hive. But unlike his brethren, there was a magical quality to Swarm that caused him to grow much larger than the rest of his kind. No longer able to fit amongst the rest of his colony, the young prince broke the long standing tradition and stepped out into the open world - where his size and strength would be put to good use in the legendary battle between the Giants and the Arkeyans.
swarm.personality: Swarm is as adventurous as he is unique. He always adds a barbed insult to a stinging attack. He never gets caught short of ideas, always having a 'plan bee' up his sleeve.
swarm.gameplay: Swarm uses his Barb Blades for melee slashes and can take flight with Flight of the Wasp to rain down stingers from above. He can transform into a Swarm Form to damage enemies on contact. His upgrades allow him to sharpen his barbs, fly faster, and fire tracking butt stinger missiles. In the 3DS version, he gains unique moves like Charged Air Blades and Explosive Stingers as he levels up.

abilities.name: Barb Blades
abilities.description: Press the Attack 1 button to slash enemies.

abilities.name: Flight of the Wasp
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 to hover in the air. While flying, press Attack 1 to shoot Barb Blades.

abilities.name: Sharpened Barbs
abilities.description: Barb Blades melee attacks do increased damage.

abilities.name: Wingin' It
abilities.description: Can fly faster and for longer durations.

abilities.name: Swarm Form
abilities.description: Press Attack 3 to turn into a swarm of bugs which damage everything they touch.

abilities.name: Stinger Shot
abilities.description: Hold Attack 1 to charge up and release to shoot a stinging energy blast.

abilities.name: Bee is for the Butt Stinger
abilities.description: While flying, press Attack 3 to fire butt stinger missiles that track enemies.

abilities.name: Razor Wings
abilities.description: Wings damage any enemies they touch.

abilities.name: Better Barb Blast
abilities.description: Barb Blades shot while flying do increased damage.

abilities.name: Ultimate Barbs
abilities.description: All Barb Blade attacks do maximum damage.

abilities.name: Swarm Storm
abilities.description: Swarm Form is bigger and does increased damage.

abilities.name: Insectsplosion
abilities.description: While in Swarm Form, press Attack 2 to do shockwave damage.

abilities.name: Bee Cleaver
abilities.description: While in Swarm Form, press Attack 1 to form a giant axe and swing at enemies.

trivia: Some of Swarm's prototype names include Giant Hornet, Wasp Man, and Bug Giant.
Swarm speaks in a Spanish accent, though the original inspiration was an Italian voice actor, who couldn't be hired due to SAG-AFTRA restrictions.
He has the lowest health out of the other Giants.
During Giants's early development, Swarm's abilities/upgrades were differently named.
'Barb Blades' was called 'Barb Blade / Barb Bullets.'
'Sharpened Barbs' was called 'Wasp Blade.' 'Wingin' It' was called 'Aerial Throttle.'
'Swarm Form' was called 'Insect Shroud Form.'
'Stinger Shot' was called 'Air Cutter.'
'Better Barb Blast' was called 'Barb Blast.'
'Ultimate Barbs' was called 'Fury Barbs.'
'Swarm Storm' was called 'Wasp Shroud Storm.'
'Insectsplosion' was called 'Wasp Shroud Shockwave.'
'Bee Cleaver' was called 'Wasp Shroud Axe.'
'Bee is for Butt Stinger' was called 'Butt Stinger Missile.'
Unlike most flying Skylanders, Swarm (and Gill Grunt) flies in a standing position rather than in a quadruped stance. However, Swarm can slightly turn during the process of flight.
He and Drobot are the only two Skylanders who can damage enemies by just flying.
There is a glitch where if Swarm enters a cutscene or is otherwise interrupted whilst flying, he will land but will still be showing the animation of his wings buzzing.
He, Hot Dog and Bumble Blast are the only Skylanders with bee related moves.

tae-kwon-crow.name: Tae Kwon Crow
tae-kwon-crow.description: Tae Kwon Crow, formerly known as the Great Hawkmongous, is a ninja crow who first appeared as one of the Dark trappable villains in Skylanders: Trap Team. He later became a Fire element Sensei in Skylanders: Imaginators.
tae-kwon-crow.biography: Tae Kwon Crow was once the leader of a villainous band of air pirates in Skyhighlands. But pirating was never his true passion. All that really mattered to him was stopping anyone that 'dared' to do anything that he deemed out of character. After he was captured by the Trap Masters, Master Eon dared him to change his ways and use his abilities for good instead. At first, Tae Kwon Crow was angry, but he soon realized that he could actually serve as a role model to young Ninjas and help them avoid the dark path that he went down. Forsaking his katana for the more traditional roundhouse fire-kick, Tae Kwon Crow now defends Skylands from whoever dares threaten it.
tae-kwon-crow.personality: Tae Kwon Crow's Imaginators backstory implies he might have OCD (obsessive compulsive disorder), constantly desiring for things to be done the way he thinks is right, even if other people are the ones acting out of line, to the point of obsession. He is known to be dramatic and takes his role as a 'role model' very seriously.
tae-kwon-crow.gameplay: In Skylanders: Trap Team, Tae Kwon Crow uses his ninja abilities to teleport and uses his katana for offense. In Skylanders: Imaginators, he uses fire-based roundhouse kicks and throwing stars. He can summon Buzzer Beaks to fight for him, which can be enraged by kicking them. His Fire Kick leaves behind a wall of fire that can ignite his shurikens for extra damage. He offers two distinct upgrade paths: Shuriken Slinger for long-range mastery or Crow-mmando for close-quarters kick combos and more crow companions.

abilities.name: Shuriken Throw
abilities.description: Press Attack 1 to throw ninja stars at nearby enemies.

abilities.name: Flame Kick
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 to do a spin kick, lighting the ground on fire.

abilities.name: Ricochet Shot
abilities.description: Your Shuriken Throw ninja stars now deal more damage and bounce between nearby enemies.

abilities.name: Buzzer Beak
abilities.description: Press Attack 3 to spawn a Buzzer Beak to fight for you.

abilities.name: Ignite Shurikens
abilities.description: Throw ninja stars through your flame wall to increase their damage.

abilities.name: Fire Beak
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 to kick your Buzzer Beak enraging it to be faster and more damaging.

abilities.name: Big Momma
abilities.description: Press and hold Attack 3 to call down the Big Momma Buzzer Beak.

abilities.name: Final Fire Flurry
abilities.description: The ultimate Sensei attack! Hold Special Attack to perform your Sky-Chi Power! Use Left Stick to aim your shurikens!

abilities.name: Triple Shurikens
abilities.description: Press Attack 1 to throw 3 ninja stars.

abilities.name: Shuriken Flurry
abilities.description: Press and hold Attack 1 for a short time to throw a flurry of 5 big shurikens.

abilities.name: Ground Saws
abilities.description: Press and hold Attack 1 longer to throw a pair of ground saws.

abilities.name: Triple Kicks
abilities.description: Press Attack 2 thrice to perform a Flame Kick combo.

abilities.name: Buzzer Battalion
abilities.description: Press Attack 3 to spawn 3 Buzzer Beaks to fight for you.

abilities.name: Fury Beak
abilities.description: Your enraged Buzzer Beaks are even faster, do even more damage, and disappear with an explosion.

trivia: He is the second trappable villain who changes his name (the first being Threatpack).
He is the only bird villain with featureless eyes.
His name is a play on 'tae kwon do', a Korean martial art. At the start of his Sky Chi, he says 'Junbi!', which means 'ready' in Korean.
Tae Kwon Crow is the only Ninja Sensei with a visible mouth.
He is one of six Villains who do not try to persuade the Portal Master into capturing them.
While most characters have one or two words in their names, Tae Kwon Crow is the first with three.
His villain quest is considered one of the hardest to complete.

template-template.name: Template Template
template-template.description: Template Template is a debug character used in various Vicarious Visions titles, characterized as a simple humanoid figure with large hands and a tail.
template-template.biography: Template Template is used as a debug character and can be found in various Vicarious Visions titles, first seen in Skylanders: Swap Force. He is a humanoid character with no particular details aside from large hands and a tail. In Skylanders: Swap Force, using a glitch, he can be seen in-game. He has three attacks (two tail spin moves and ineffective slaps) and a full, though placeholder, upgrade tree. He cannot attack enemies but can be attacked and swapped with. His element HUD is not rendered, revealing parts of the health and XP gauges. His movement type is Climb (or Rocket on Player 2), but he cannot participate in SWAP Force Zones. His portrait is a 'PLACEHOLDER' puff of smoke, except during battle results screen where he instead uses Magna Charge's portrait. During the summoning sequence or 'Magic Moment', Template Template is incorrectly described as a Fire element Skylander. In Skylanders: SuperChargers, he appears in the mainline version with a generic placeholder icon and lacks a 3D preview. In Skylanders: Imaginators, his summon animation causes a crash, though his bottom half can be summoned with another Skylander's top half without crashing (except in racing mode where he can participate). If taken from racing mode to the main game without a summoning sequence, the game won't crash. His icon is Stink Bomb's, except in racing setup where it's a red exclamation mark. In the Nintendo Switch version, he remains in files but cannot be summoned without modification due to the lack of racing mode.
template-template.personality: As a debug character, Template Template lacks a distinct narrative personality, serving primarily as a functional placeholder for testing game mechanics, animations, and facial expressions.
template-template.gameplay: Template Template has three attacks: two different tail spin moves and a series of ineffective slaps. He possesses five of the normal nine quests and a full upgrade tree, which is placeholder and grants no upgrades. He is unable to attack enemies but can be attacked. Other Skylanders with the Swap ability can swap with him. His element HUD is not rendered due to lacking an element. His movement type is Climb (or Rocket on Player 2), but he cannot participate in SWAP Force Zones. In Imaginators, his summon animation crashes the game unless only his bottom half is summoned with another Skylander's top half, or if he's taken from racing mode to the main game without a summoning sequence. He is able to participate in racing mode in Imaginators.

trivia: His name refers to his use as the base for Swap Force Skylanders, indicating both of his top and bottom half.
Though he doesn't seem to be a placeholder for any particular Swap Force character, his overall body shape and movement most resembles that of the officially released Skylander, Fire Kraken.
Template Template's head most resembles that of an earless Greeble.
They share some animations with Free Ranger (such as his primary attack).
Template Template's traversal animations are used by the Jet swapper half when it is dismounted from the board.
Template Template slides around if any attacks are done whilst moving, due to the lack of any partial/alternative animations for them.
Template Template is also used as a placeholder in Vicarious Visions' storyboards, representing the in-engine Skylander.

Template Template possesses happy, angry, and goofy facial animations. However, he is missing a sad animation (which typically appears on other Skylanders from Swap Force), causing his emotion to reset back to normal when pressed.
His victory animation for Battle Mode uses the idle animation for another template character, Template Legacy, causing his body to shrink down considerably.
Template Template's materials are not present in the Wii version of Swap Force, resulting in a fully white appearance.

Template Template can be seen as part of two development screenshots present in the files for Swap Force, SuperChargers, and Imaginators. These images are stored as raw PNG files rather than in archives. Both screenshots also contain the Utah Teapot, a common test geometry used in rendering.
Template Template was originally fully blue instead of green, as seen in a GDC Vault Presentation.

terrabite.name: Terrabite
terrabite.description: Terrabite is one of the four Sidekicks in Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure. He is the miniature version of Terrafin, eventually becoming a Mini Skylander in Skylanders: Trap Team.
terrabite.biography: Within the Skylands, a realm of infinite possibilities, there is in fact an alternate reality known as the Skylands Miniverse. Everything there is smaller, including the Skylanders. The Skylanders Sidekicks come from that Miniverse and have traveled to the Skylands to meet their regular-sized alter egos and tag along with them on adventures. The Skylander Minis started off as regular 'Sidekicks', assisting the Skylanders on many exciting adventures. And what they lacked in size they more than made up for in courage. Ultimately determined to become full-fledged heroes, they trained at the Skylands Academy - honing their powers and skills until they were ready. Now, they stand side by side with their full grown counterparts, ready to defend Skylands against Kaos and his evil minions.
terrabite.personality: Terrabite is pretty persistent. If he gets knocked down, he gets right back up again in true hero style.
terrabite.gameplay: Terrabite acts as a miniature version of Terrafin. Originally introduced as a Sidekick that followed the player's character, he transitioned into a fully playable Mini Skylander in Skylanders: Trap Team. His moveset mirrors Terrafin's, focusing on physical brawling and earth-based maneuvers like burrowing underground to evade enemies and launch surprise attacks.

abilities.name: Shark Punch
abilities.description: Terrabite punches enemies with his fists.

abilities.name: Earth Swim
abilities.description: Terrabite dives into the ground and swims through the earth to avoid damage and strike from below.

abilities.name: Brass Knuckles
abilities.description: Provides increased damage for the Shark Punch attack.

abilities.name: Mega Bellyflop
abilities.description: While earth swimming, jump out of the ground to perform a powerful belly flop.

abilities.name: Razorfin
abilities.description: Terrabite's fin deals damage to enemies while he is earth swimming.

trivia: Terrabite's name is a play on the word Terabyte, referring to a unit of information that is equal to one million million bytes (or 2^40).
As a sidekick in Spyro's Adventure to Swap Force, Terrabite had spikes on his head. As a Mini Skylander in Trap Team onward, his spikes are not featured.
Strangely, in his promo art and toy figure, Terrabite's spikes are black. In-game, they are orange.
Terrabite was voiced by Joey Camen in 2012.

terrafin.name: Terrafin
appearances: Trigger Happy Targets the Evil Kaos
terrafin.description: Terrafin is a dirt shark Skylander in Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure who was first available only in the Pirate Seas Adventure Pack. He is of the Earth element.
terrafin.biography: Terrafin hails from The Dirt Seas, where it was common to swim, bathe, and even snorkel beneath the ground. But a powerful explosion in the sky created a blast wave that turned the ocean of sand into a vast sheet of glass, putting an end to Terrafin's duty as the local lifeguard. Not one to stay idle, the brawny dirt shark found himself training in the art of boxing, and not long after he was local champ. Fighters came from all around to challenge him, but it was a chance meeting with a great Portal Master that led him to give up his title for a greater purpose.
terrafin.personality: Terrafin is a strong fighter and has a personality to match. He's rough and physically minded, and blunt in his dealings with others. His comments in the various Skylander videos suggest that he's got a personality based on B.A. Baracus from the A-Team TV series. He often states he's both a fighter and a lover. Nothing gets Terrafin on the ropes. If he's knocked down he gets straight back up again, coming back fighting from any scrap. He thinks with his fists, and sometimes his teeth. Terrafin may be a little rough and ready, but he's always ready to use his mighty shark-fists to protect the innocent.
terrafin.gameplay: Like all dirt sharks, Terrafin can swim and burrow through the ground. Being a former tournament boxer, he can perform punches and use his ground abilities to deal the finishing blow on his enemies. In the 'Mask of Power' series it was shown that Terrafin is strong enough to punch away an incoming cannonball as if it was a beach ball.

abilities.name: Spiked Knuckles
abilities.description: All Punch attacks do even MORE damage.

abilities.description: Terrafin launches mini-sharks at enemies who damage him.

trivia: Terrafin's name is a play on terrapin, a type of freshwater turtle.
His name also contains 'Terra' (The Latin/Italian/Portuguese term for Earth or land) and 'Fin' (as in a shark fin).
A turtle-like Character from 'Ben 10 : Ultamite Alien' with a similar name, 'Terraspin' is also a play on 'Terrapin'.

One time Terrafin and Doom Stone had a contest to see who was the strongest, Terrafin started by lifting a huge boulder. Doom Stone then lifted the boulder but with only one hand. Terrafin then lifted both Doom Stone and the boulder, then Doom Stone began juggling Terrafin and the boulder. Eventually they settled on an arm wrestling contest, but after 4 days of arm wrestling, they both quit.
He may be one of the toughest of all Skylanders, but Terrafin is afraid of flying.
His powerful jaws can chomp through hard stone.
Terrafin was originally called Finn in the early beta gameplay of Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure.
While swimming underground using his Earth Swim attack, Terrafin hums 3 different songs. which some people think one of them sounds similar to Lady Gaga's song, Bad Romance.
In his earlier promotional art, Terrafin is shown to be blue and white, but yet in his toy form and in the game he is gray and white.
According to Terrafin in 'The Beginning' trailer, Kaos owes him five dollars.
In the Toy Fair 2011 debut trailer of Spyro's Adventure, Terrafin's toy form is different from the final version.
Terrafin is one of the ten Skylanders who can summon helpers (others include Sonic Boom, Double Trouble, Warnado, Pop Fizz, and Eye-Brawl).
There is a glitch where while burrowing underground with Terrafin, if you happen to burrow underneath food, he will eat it (once you get his Soul Gem Ability) but his health will not replenish.
Despite being a Dirt Shark, Terrafin doesn't possess a tail, which is a trait commonly seen on most dirt shark inhabitants seen in Skylanders: Swap Force, making him the only dirt shark to do so.
He is the only Adventure Pack Skylander to not have an evil version of him in Skylanders: Spyro's Adventure.
He is also the only Adventure Pack Skylander to recieve a Series 3 and SuperCharger release.
He and Slam Bam are the only adventure pack Skylanders to not be part of the forgotten eight.
When Terrafin swims underground, he is invulnerable to most attacks for a short period of time. However, in Trap Team, Terrafin's invulnerability while digging has been removed.

thrillipede.name: Thrillipede
thrillipede.description: Thrillipede is a green millipede who is one of the Life SuperChargers in Skylanders: SuperChargers. His signature vehicle is the Buzz Wing.
thrillipede.biography: Thrillipede served in the Millipede Military in the outer regions of Skylands. As the top pilot in his unit, Thrillipede was responsible for single-handedly blasting over 300 Greeble warships out of the sky! When the Great Greeble War came to an end, he returned to his hometown of Flutter Bay as a celebrated hero. He was the talk of the town and everyone wanted to shake the many hands of the famous young pilot. News of his heroics eventually made their way to Captain Flynn at the Skylanders Academy, who set out to determine if the stories were true. In a series of friendly challenges, the two pilots raced, soared through obstacles, and performed incredible stunts in front of a cheering Flutter Bay crowd. In each event, Thrillipede stood victorious, and was asked to join the Skylanders shortly after. Of course, Flynn later admitted that he 'let him win' so that Thrillipede wouldn't be embarrassed in front of his hometown.
thrillipede.personality: Thrillipede is incredibly skilled in combat, but is very reserved when not battling evil. Despite not being a bird, he is very observant when riding his Buzz Wing, and has great knowledge on flight mechanics. In his SuperCharger Quest, he is also shown to be very modest, and holds a longstanding friendship with Buzz. Thrillipede flies fearless through the skies, zipping through the air without a care. He's committed to his duty, but freely admits he loves to wow the crowds.
thrillipede.gameplay: Thrillipede is a combat specialist described as a 'pitching machine for grenades.' He excels in aerial mechanics when paired with his vehicle, the Buzz Wing. In gameplay, he uses cocoon grenades (Bug Bombs) to slow enemies and delivers physical strikes with his four arms. He can wrap himself in a defensive cocoon to absorb damage before detonating outward, and his advanced upgrades allow him to sprout wings for aerial bombardment or deploy stacking insect swarms that spread between enemies.

trivia: His Soul Gem shares a name with Beautifly, a creature from Pokémon.
Strangely, although Thrillipede can wrap himself in a cocoon with his Cocooned ability, millipedes do not cocoon themselves.
Thrillipede possesses wings in later upgrades, but millipedes in real life don't actually have wings.
He, Slam Bam and Starcast are the only Skylanders who have four arms.
Thrillipede's voice actor is Patrick Seitz, who also voices Hot Head, Rip Tide, and Chomp Chest.
He is the only Life SuperCharger without a dark edition counterpart and the only one not included in a starter pack.
Thrillipede is the only new SuperCharger who did not appear in Skylanders: Ring of Heroes.
Thrillipede was unreleased in the US for an unknown reason, though his vehicle and Easter variant were released.
Concept art included alternative designs as a legless moth, an armored beetle, and a slender dragonfly.
Developer David A. Rodriguez described him as 'like a pitching machine... for grenades.'

thumpback.name: Thumpback
thumpback.description: Thumpback is a large blue whale-like creature, with small white eyes, a blowhole on the top of his head and a large mouth with small pointed teeth inside. He also has muscular arms with coral and barnacle growing on them, and white claws on his fingers and feet. He wears a brown belt around his waist, with a small boat navigator as the buckle, and silver shoulder pads. He even carries a large anchor as his weapon.
thumpback.biography: Thumpback was once a crew member of The Phantom Tide, the most fearsome pirate ship in all of Skylands. But the actual pirating part about being a pirate didn't interest Thumpback so much as the benefits that came with traveling on a large ship. After all, his real passion was fishing. But when his chance came to finally ensnare the most elusive creature in the sky - the Leviathan Cloud Crab - he was pulled over board and carried off into the horizon. This was actually quite fortunate, because sometime later The Phantom Tide and its entire crew were banished to the Chest of Exile. Thumpback’s pirating days were over, but his legend as one of the first Skylanders had only just begun.
thumpback.personality: Thumpback is steadfast, dependable, trustworthy, and gifted with the patience of an angler.
thumpback.gameplay: Thumpback is a Water Giant who focuses on heavy anchor attacks and belly-sliding maneuvers. In the console version, his primary Anchor Assault can be executed in various combos, while his Belly Flop allows him to slide across the battlefield, damaging enemies in his path. His Chomp ability allows for high-damage melee bites. On the 3DS, he possesses a grappling iron ability to pull enemies toward him and a "Whalecopter" move for extra air time.

trivia: It is rumored that six fully grown Skylanders could fit inside Thumpback's mouth, not that they'd want to.
Thumpback, Ninjini, and Crusher are the only three Giants to have weapons that are not a part of their bodies.
Thumpback and Wash Buckler are the only two Skylanders who were once part of a gang of pirates.
Thumpback's name is a combination of "Thump" and "Humpback".
According to Lou Studdert, Thumpback was originally called Big Mouth Whale.
He speaks with a Thick Scottish accent in gameplay. But on most trailers and commercials he spoke in an American accent.
Thumpback is based on a Humpback Whale. But he instead has pointed teeth in his mouth, while real humpback whales have baleen.

thumpling.name: Thumpling
thumpling.description: Thumpling is one of the four Sidekicks in Skylanders: Giants. He is the miniature version of the giant Thumpback, eventually becoming a Mini Skylander in Skylanders: Trap Team.
thumpling.biography: Within the Skylands, a realm of infinite possibilities, there is in fact an alternate reality known as the Skylands Miniverse. Everything there is smaller, including the Skylanders. The Skylanders Sidekicks come from that Miniverse and have traveled to the Skylands to meet their regular-sized alter egos and tag along with them on adventures. The Skylander Minis started off as regular 'Sidekicks', assisting the Skylanders on many exciting adventures. And what they lacked in size they more than made up for in courage. Ultimately determined to become full-fledged heroes, they trained at the Skylands Academy - honing their powers and skills until they were ready. Now, they stand side by side with their full grown counterparts, ready to defend Skylands against Kaos and his evil minions.
thumpling.personality: Thumpling is a dedicated hero who will always be there whenever his teammates need him. He shares Thumpback's love for fishing.
thumpling.gameplay: Thumpling's statistics in-game for health and speed are often unlisted, but his official Power Stats are high, with 90 Strength and 90 Defense, and a perfect 100 in Agility and Luck. These Power Stats are provided for completeness and are not actively used in the gameplay mechanics of the series.

trivia: His name is most likely a pun on the food 'dumpling'.
His pedestal has a small wavy splash in front of him, while most Water pedestals have a uniform wave pattern around the character.
He is the second Skylander to named after a food; the first being Hot Dog and the third being Pop Thorn.

In Skylanders: Lost Islands, Thumpling seems to be much smaller than Barkley, Eye-Small, and Mini Jini despite being the Mini version of a Giant. Because of the way the game's Skylander section worked, it was easier to select him through the list than to try and pick him up on the overworld.
In Skylanders Issue 3, while being attacked by Kaos's trolls, Thumpling calls himself a 'shark'.

thunderbolt.name: Thunderbolt
thunderbolt.description: Thunderbolt is one of the two Air Trap Masters in Skylanders: Trap Team.
thunderbolt.biography: Epically strong and heroically competitive, Thunderbolt grew up on legendary Mount Cloudpierce. Every year, his people held a contest to determine who would wield the Storm Sword – a legendary blade with the power to change the seasons in Skylands. To Thunderbolt, this would be a great honor. But on the day he won the contest and was about to be presented with the sword, a Frost Mage snatched it and plunged all of Skylands into a wintery deep-freeze. Undaunted, Thunderbolt bravely took chase. Riding twin bolts of chained lightning, he overtook the mage, reclaimed the sword, and restored balance to the weather systems in Skylands. For his heroic actions, Thunderbolt was made a member of the Trap Team, and he now uses his Traptanium Storm Sword to strike evil at every turn!
thunderbolt.personality: Thunderbolt is a fierce competitor who faces each opponent with honor and bravery.
thunderbolt.gameplay: Thunderbolt can use his enormous Traptanium Storm Sword, which causes lightning to blast out with every swing, he can also use it to create a tornado that pulls in enemies. Thunderbolt can even shoot storm clouds from his own cloudy body which can shock enemies.

trivia: He is similar to Lightning Rod in the following characteristics: Both are Air Skylanders. Both have lower torsos composed of clouds. Both use storm and electrical type attacks. Both of their names are based on electricity.
The name of Thunderbolt's home, Mount Cloudpierce, is similar to Mount Cloudbreak.
His Soul Gem ability has the same name as Cynder's Wow Pow from Skylanders: Giants.

There is a glitch that removes Thunderbolt's cloud and makes him appear without any legs. To perform this, the player must approach the Mirror of Mystery next to the vortex. Pressing the button will allow Glumshanks to come and talk to the Skylander. The player has to press 'NO' when the prompt appears to make the cloud disappear.
In Skylanders: SuperChargers Racing, instead of his regular catchphrase, he says 'Taking the World by Storm'.

tidepool.name: Tidepool
tidepool.description: Tidepool is a marine Water Sensei of the Quickshot Battle Class in Skylanders: Imaginators.
tidepool.biography: Long before she became a Sensei, Tidepool was an undercover agent for a top secret organization known as the Aqua Marines. However, one day she was betrayed by her superiors, who were part of an even more top secret organization intent on destroying Skylands. Using her spy training, Tidepool made it her personal mission to seek out every member of this evil shadow group and bring them to justice. This did not go unnoticed by Master Eon, who felt that someone of her caliber would be perfect to train new Skylanders as a Sensei of the Quickshot class. However, Tidepool was not easily convinced that she could even trust Eon and the Skylanders after being deceived by her last organization. To earn her trust, she requested that everyone pass a truth test that she would conduct. Thankfully, all of the members of the Skylanders Academy passed with flying colors... except for Flynn, who insisted that he was 50% Mabu and 50% enchilada sauce. Tidepool felt that he was 100% meathead.
tidepool.catchphrase: In a League of My Own!
tidepool.personality: Initially untrusting, discerning, and a skilled undercover agent. She is professional, disciplined, and slightly cynical due to her past experiences. She value truth and credentials after being betrayed in her past.
tidepool.gameplay: Tidepool's gameplay centers on her dual Squid Pistols, which fire ink-based projectiles at a distance. As a Quickshot, she excels at rapid fire and keeping enemies at bay. Her abilities allow her to summon whale tails and toss squids that attack enemies independently, providing both direct damage and crowd control. Her Soul Gem ability provides defensive capabilities using her shell helmet.

abilities.description: Create a powerful whirlpool when using Whale Tale!

trivia: Tidepool's name refers to the bodies of water formed by sea tides.
Tidepool's super spy motif, combined with her British accent is very likely a direct reference to James Bond.
Tidepool's catchphrase is very likely inspired by the Jules Verne novel '20,000 Leagues Under the Sea'.
Her pistols can be obtained for Imaginators by opening the Quickshot Shrine in Sky Fortress. She also grants her shell helmet when first placed on the portal.
Her whale companions share the same character model as the dream whale floating around the outside Telescope Towers in Skylanders: Trap Team.
She is the second Water Skylander to use ink-based attacks whereas Wash Buckler is the first. Splat also uses ink, but a different kind (specifically, the ink used by artists instead of cephalopods).
Whenever she pushes blocks or other movable objects, Tidepool pushes with her pistols, which usually leaves temporary ink stains on them.
She is the only Water Sensei who is not a Brawler.
She is the only Quickshot Sensei who was not previously a Villain.
Tidepool and Spy Rise both have a motivation as secret agents.
Tidepool's Soul Gem cutscene shows a different icon to the Quickshot Battle Class, possibly a prototype design.

torch.name: Torch
torch.description: Torch is one of the Fire core Skylanders in Skylanders: Trap Team.
torch.biography: Torch's childhood was spent working with her grandfather as a dragon keeper, where she helped tend to a stable of dragons that protected her village. One year, an evil Snow Dragon unleashed a terrible blizzard that trapped her entire homeland inside a massive ice glacier! Torch was the only one to escape. Having always been fearless, she set out at once to rescue the villagers and her dragons from their chilly fate. Armed with her Firespout Flamethrower, she fought hard through the treacherous conditions and bravely defeated the Snow Dragon in an epic battle. After the village was free from its icy doom, Torch returned home to find her grandfather missing. The only token left behind was his lucky flaming horseshoe. Now as a member of the Skylanders, Torch wields her powerful flamethrower as well as her lucky horseshoe in hopes it will one day lead her to the grandfather she had lost.
torch.personality: Torch is pretty fearless. Some might say she is hotheaded.
torch.gameplay: Torch uses her Firespout Flamethrower to roast enemies with primary attacks and tosses Flaming Horseshoes as secondary attacks. She also possesses a unique Flaming Hair Whip to knock back enemies. On console, her upgrades allow her to set the ground on fire or breathe blue flames. In the 3DS version, her horse shoes catch fire on the ground and she delivers powerful hits when enemies get close.

abilities.description: Use a fire attack on a Flaming Horseshoe and it comes to life, attacking enemies.

trivia: She is the second Fire Skylander to be female, the first being Smolderdash.

Her Soul Gem upgrade, The Incinerator, has many similarities with the Incinerator from Ratchet & Clank Future: Tools of Destruction, as they're both the maximum upgrade, have dual flame jets coming out of the flamethrower, and have similar names.

Torch is one of the few Skylanders who are currently searching for their loved ones while fighting evil (others being Gill Grunt, Chill, Sprocket, and Roller Brawl). However, Roller Brawl reunited with her brothers in Biting Back by freeing them from Kaos, who ordered trolls to control them by magical puppets.
Torch's voice actor, Salli Saffioti, also voiced Whirlwind and Eye Scream.
Torch claims that the villain Hood Sickle 'gives her the creeps'.
During Gamescom 2014, some of the game's developers mispronounced her name as 'Forge'.
A skin texture map of Torch was leaked in the 1.0 version of Skylanders: Ring of Heroes, but she never appeared in the final game.

trail-blazer.name: Trail Blazer
trail-blazer.description: Trail Blazer is a fire unicorn who is one of the Fire Core Skylanders in Skylanders: Trap Team.
trail-blazer.biography: Trail Blazer was always hot tempered, especially when he saw anything as being unfair. One day, he came across another unicorn that was trapped in a net. But it wasn’t just any unicorn. It was the mythical Unocorn – a magical creature with a Churro Horn that sprinkled enchanted cinnamon throughout Skylands. Trail Blazer freed it at once. Soon after, the Dark Wizards who had set the trap returned, and were very angry to find their dastardly deed had been thwarted. But Trail Blazer was much more fired up – for it turned out the spicy cinnamon from the Churro Horn had somehow rubbed off on him and mixed with his elemental fire. So he was literally set ablaze with fury! He then ran fiery circles around the wizards, forcing them to flee and never return. After realizing his newfound fury could be used to fight evil everywhere, Trail Blazer sought out the Skylanders, who immediately welcomed him as a member.
trail-blazer.personality: Trail Blazer is a hot-tempered unicorn, being set ablaze when he saw anything unfair. However he also possesses a competitive spirit, which in one case causes him to discourage others.
trail-blazer.gameplay: Trail Blazer is a Fire element Skylander whose playstyle combines fast fire projectiles with powerful melee kicks. On console, he uses 'Fireball' and 'Roundhouse Kick', which can be upgraded into a 'Stampede!' or 'Bucking Bronco' mode. His Soul Gem, 'Heat Wave', allows for a powerful charged wave attack. In the 3DS version, his moveset differs slightly, featuring 'Mane of Fire' and 'Bad Bronco', with the ability to summon spectral fire stallions. His stats highlight high agility and speed, making him a mobile offensive threat.

trivia: His catchphrase is a play on the phrase, 'The main event'.
One of his battle cries is shared by Spyro's catchphrase, 'All Fired Up!' Meanwhile, one of his basic upgrades is the same with Spitfire's catchphrase, 'Fuel the Fire!'

He, Knight Mare and Whirlwind are currently the only equestrian-based Skylanders. He and Whirlwind are the only ones to be unicorn-based. Oddly enough, in the Tall Tales trailer for Giants, it implies that unicorns don't exist in Skylands, despite the fact that Trail Blazer is a unicorn.
Trail Blazer is voiced by Yuri Lowenthal, who also voiced Fright Rider and Softpaw in the series.
When driving in SuperChargers, he grabs the wheel with his mouth to drive.
Both Pain-Yatta and Trail Blazer came across the Unocorn, and the latter frees it not long after the piñata lost his friend.
Trail Blazer's defeat animation was changed between Trap Team and SuperChargers. In Trap Team, he collapses onto his side, whereas in SuperChargers, he sits down like a dog.

trap-shadow.name: Trap Shadow
trap-shadow.description: Trap Shadow is a sabre-toothed tiger hunter who is one of the SWAP Force Skylanders in Skylanders: Swap Force.
trap-shadow.biography: Once part of an elite tribe of hunters in a remote area of Skylands, Trap Shadow used his cat-like cunning, ingenious traps and mystical stealth abilities to catch nearly everything that could be caught. As a result, his fame around Skylands grew so much that it attracted the attention of an evil cadre of wizards. They plotted to capture Trap Shadow and use his abilities to ensnare the most uncatchable thing of all - Master Eon himself. But Trap Shadow could sense them coming from miles away. Outsmarted and outmaneuvered, each of the wizards was easily captured by Trap Shadow's bewildering array of traps and snares until they were all locked away for good. Having saved Master Eon, he quickly made Trap Shadow a Skylander.
trap-shadow.personality: The finest feline tracker of his tribe, Trap Shadow was the go-to cat if you wanted something caught. He mostly keeps to himself. However, since becoming a Skylander, he's been trying to become a team player. You have to get up early to catch Trap Shadow out - as the wicked wizards discovered. He sniffed out their plans and trapped them before they could trap him (or Eon, for that matter).
trap-shadow.gameplay: Trap Shadow attacks by slashing enemies with his shadowy claws, and can kick waves of shadows at foes. He can also throw magical traps that snap and damage enemies, and even turn invisible by using shadows, and create an explosion of shadows when reappearing.

abilities.name: Bumps in the Night
abilities.description: Shade Steps do increased damage. Huh? Who's footprints are these?

trivia: After purchasing his Soul Gem ability, 'Shadow Striker', Trap Shadow wears his green bandanna over his muzzle, instead of around his neck.
His catchphrase is a pun on 'hide and seek'.
When he turns invisible, his eyes glow purple, but in the Sneak SWAP Zone, he will fully vanish while leaving his purple aura shown at the bottom and shadowy paw prints.
His appearance has some of the features of a saber-tooth cat (long fangs), panther (facial features), and tiger (fur color patterns).

He is the second SWAP Force Skylander with the ability to turn invisible, but only when his Soul Gem ability, 'Living Shadow', is purchased. If not, enemies and bosses will spot him. Also, he stays invisible much shorter than Stink Bomb and can do so while the second attack button is held down.
He is the only SWAP Force Skylander on the 3DS with no dash attack upgrade.

He has many abilities that would later be associated with the Dark Element, such as hiding in shadows and using dark magic. Oddly, these abilities were associated with Undead Skylanders (such as Cynder) at the time of Swap Force's release, not Magic.
Trap Shadow was one of the many Skylanders planned to appear in Skylanders: Ring of Heroes. Before the game's closure, only concept art of his Awakened Form was released.
While Trap Shadow is in stealth mode, the music, ambient sounds, and dialogues become muted.
On his toy from, his top half shows him holding a snap trap in his right hand, and the left one held up, with his index finger up to his mouth, as if saying, 'Ssshhh!'
In the animated intro to his Soul Gem, Trap Shadow's eyes appear a much more vivid green than they do in-game or in his art.

trap-team.name: Trap Team
trap-team.description: The Trap Team, individually referred to as Trap Masters, are a group of Skylanders who use special crystallized weapons to weaken Villains in Skylanders: Trap Team. Their weaponry is crafted from Traptanium, allowing them to harness the power of the crystals to defeat the most notorious criminals in Skylands. When near a Traptanium crystal cluster or when facing a trappable Villain, their Traptanium weaponry glows brightly.
trap-team.biography: The Trap Masters were the ones who originally caught and imprisoned the villains, including the notorious Doom Raiders, in Cloudcracker Prison. They were the original guardians of the prison until Kaos blew up the walls with a blast of concentrated Evil, which caused the Trap Masters to be banished to Earth alongside the shards of Traptanium. On Earth, they wait for a Portal Master to help them return to Skylands and recapture the escaped villains.
trap-team.catchphrase: The Trap Masters use special crystallized weapons to weaken Villains.
trap-team.personality: The Trap Team is a group of dedicated and powerful protectors of Skylands. As the former wardens of Cloudcracker Prison, they are unified by their duty to capture escaped villains. While the team consists of various individuals with unique traits, they are characterized by their natural leadership—with Snap Shot often acting as their primary leader—and their commitment to using their Traptanium weapons for the greater good.
trap-team.gameplay: Trap Masters utilize Traptanium weaponry that glows when in proximity to Traptanium crystals or trappable villains. In the console version of Skylanders: Trap Team, they are the only Skylanders capable of opening Elemental Gates. In the Nintendo 3DS version, they have access to a special power called Trap Attack, which is executed by filling a gauge with Traptanium shards. Additionally, when using Villains, the Trap Masters provide a timer that drains slower and recharges faster.

abilities.name: Traptanium Weaponry
abilities.description: The Trap Masters use specialized crystallized weapons made of Traptanium to weaken and capture villains. These weapons glow brightly when near a Traptanium crystal cluster or when facing a trappable Villain.

abilities.name: Trap Attack
abilities.description: A unique powerful attack used in the 3DS version of the game. It is activated by filling a trap gauge with Traptanium shards collected from defeated enemies or destroyed objects. It is similar to the Sky-Chi from Skylanders: Imaginators.

trivia: The Trap Team were originally called Crystal Warriors during development.
Each Trap Master has the Trap Team symbol somewhere on their attire or bodies.
Because the Trap Team's weapons are made of Traptanium, they are the same color as the elemental trap they represent.
In toy form, Trap Masters are almost about the same size as the Giants.
Gearshift, Head Rush, Tuff Luck, and Knight Mare are the only female Trap Masters.
Out of all the Trap Masters, Blastermind and Short Cut are the shortest.
When used with Villains, they get a timer that drains slower, but recharges faster.
Trap Masters are the only Skylanders that can open Elemental Gates in Skylanders: Trap Team. This does not apply to the 3DS version.
Snap Shot, Lob-Star, Gearshift, Gusto, and Ka-Boom are the only Trap Masters to use long-range weaponry.
The Trap Attack from the Nintendo 3DS version is similar to the Sky-Chi from Skylanders: Imaginators. Both are unique powerful attacks for every Skylander, which are tied to an gauge.
Jawbreaker and Snap Shot are the only Trap Masters to have more than one alternate counterpart. Each one having an Alt Deco figure and an Alter Ego, and Snap Shot having an Instant counterpart.

Strangely, Wallop is shown to serve as the leader in most trailers, commercials and in the introduction of the game. This isn't true however, as Snap Shot is really the natural leader of the Trap Masters.

tread-head.name: Tread Head
tread-head.description: Tread Head is one of the Tech Skylanders introduced in Skylanders: Trap Team.
tread-head.biography: As an orphan from the Dizzying Dunes, Tread Head had always dreamed of racing. And after a summer of scavenging for parts, he finally managed to build a bike that would allow him to enter the local racing circuit. The other competitors laughed at the crudeness of his work, but Tread Head had built it for performance, not for style. So when the race began, he jumped out to a commanding lead. But as he entered a canyon, he suddenly found himself at a roadblock – of Goblin troops! Knowing the other racers were in danger, he pulled off the road and kicked up so much dust that the Goblins had no choice but to flee, allowing the other racers to pass safely. Tread Head may have lost the race that day, but he earned the respect of Master Eon, who would see to it that Tread Head would tread on evil wherever he goes!
tread-head.personality: Tread Head prefers substance over style. It's what inside that matters the most. The outside is just for show.
tread-head.gameplay:
Skylanders can use abilities depending on their level.

Starting Powers

Steamroll Smash (Primary Attack): Hold (Y) to jump forward and roll over anything in range.
Exhaust Blast (Secondary Attack): Press (X) to shoot fire from the exhaust.
Upgrades

Full Steamroll Smash (requires level: 3): Steamroll now has 4 levels. Releasing the button with the right timing will do a front flip for extra damage. Releasing too late will have the bike fall backwards.
Flame Circle (requires level: 6): Repeatedly press (Y) to spin frantically, and eventually trigger a flamethrower.
Rocket (requires level: 9): Hold (X) to charge-up then release to shoot forward like a rocket and damage everything ahead.

trivia: Tread Head is one of the few Skylanders who aren't Superchargers but use vehicles as weapons (other examples are Sprocket and Fryno). However, he is the first and currently the only one to never get off his ride.
He and High Five both have a racing theme.
The only time he is seen out of his vehicle is in his rest cutscene, where he gets out as it breaks down.
In Skylanders: SuperChargers, if you put him in another Vehicle, he will get out of his own bike and drive the vehicle he is driving.
Tread Head shares many physical similarities with Air Strike, including proportions, stature and facial features.
If Tread Head jumps while in wheelie mode, he’ll do a backflip with his bike.
When given a hat, it appears much smaller on him compared to on other Skylanders. This is most likely to avoid having it clip through his bike.
Unlike other playable characters, when the player stops moving the control stick, Tread Head won’t stop moving right away, as he has to slow his bike to a stop.

However, if the player presses the jump button, moves the control stick in the direction they want to go, then lets go before Tread Head hits the ground, he will land in place, just like every other playable character.

tree-rex.name: Tree Rex
tree-rex.description: Tree Rex is a colossal Ent who is a Life Skylander and one of the eight Giants in Skylanders: Giants. He is available exclusively in the Skylanders: Giants Starter Pack and Portal Owners Pack.
tree-rex.biography: Long ago before the Giants protected Skylands, Tree Rex was a majestic tree living peacefully in the ancient woods. But this tranquil peace came to an end when the Arkeyans built a nearby factory to produce war machines. After years of his soil being poisoned by the magic and tech waste from the factory, he mutated into who he is now - a powerful Giant who will crush anything that threatens the natural order of things.
tree-rex.personality: Tree Rex is a natural protector who is as wise as he is majestic, unwavering in his mission to protect Skylands from evil magic. He has also dedicated his life to maintain the natural balance of all things.
tree-rex.gameplay: Tree Rex can smash his arm against the ground to crush enemies, and create massive shockwaves. When upgraded further, he can make his arm grow thorns, and cause even larger shockwaves. He can also charge at enemies and crush enemies with his elbow, and shoot solar beams at opponents. In Skylanders: Battlecast, he is able to grow roots to restore his own health while increasing his maximum amount, being a formidable tank. His Special Ability is Overgrowth, increasing his max health, and his signature Gear is the Thorncaster, randomly increasing the cost of enemy spells.

trivia: Tree Rex's name is a pun on the giant dinosaur, T. Rex, also known as Tyrannosaurus Rex.
Tree Rex's soul gem is a woodpecker nested on his back that pecks nearby enemies to death.
Tree Rex is voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson, who also voices Stump Smash. Coincidentally, both Skylanders are trees of the Life element.
Despite the rumors, counting his rings will not tell you Tree Rex's age.
His catchphrase is a pun on 'Be Afraid of the Dark!'.
Tree Rex was the first Giant revealed for Skylanders: Giants.
One of his battle cries, 'Bouncy Bouncy!' is the name of one of Eye-Brawl's upgrades.
He and Cynder are the only Skylanders to have an ally follow them continuously via Soul Gems in the Giants Starter Pack.
He, Thumpback, Eye-Brawl, and Ninjini are the only Giants who have Minis.
His name was first used for 3DS versions of Stump Demons.
In early versions of Giants, Tree Rex has green eyes, but in concept art and the final version his eyes are blue.
Tree Rex's attacks all use his right arm, except for his Soul Gem.
There is a glitch in the Wii version of SWAP Force where his Woodpecker Pal will sometimes not appear.
Tree Rex was planned for the second season of Skylanders Academy, but he was cut for budget reasons.

tri-tip.name: Tri-Tip
tri-tip.description: Tri-Tip is an Earth-elemental Triceratops who is one of the Smasher Senseis in Skylanders: Imaginators. He wields a massive mace and wears black and gold armor adorned with the golden Sensei belt.
tri-tip.biography: Long before he became a Sensei, Tri-Tip wandered Skylands searching for the mythical Warping Walnut Tree, rumored to never be at the same place long before moving to a new location. After many years, he found the tree - and just before it vanished once again, he took from it a Golden Walnut, which was said to reveal life's purpose to those who could open it. But to his dismay, the enchanted walnut could not be cracked no matter how hard he struck it with his thick head. Realizing that only a weapon of immense power could crack the magical shell, and not his head, Tri-Tip forged a mighty mace and trained with the greatest warriors to become the ultimate Master of Smashing. But on the day when he was finally ready to open the shell, he paused. It was then that Tri-Tip realized his true purpose – one that the unopened walnut had been teaching him all along. His purpose in life was to use his skills to protect Skylands. He then gifted the unopened walnut to one of his students and left to join the Skylanders.
tri-tip.personality: Determined and reflective, Tri-Tip spent years focused on a single goal before realizing his true calling was to protect others. He possesses a disciplined warrior's spirit tempered by a sense of duty to Skylands. He is also known to have a bit of humor, jokingly admitting to 'stealing' catchphrases from other dinosaur Skylanders.
tri-tip.gameplay: Tri-Tip is a powerful Smasher Sensei who uses his mace for devastating ground smashes and his horns for charging through enemies. He can strategically control the battlefield using fossil traps and call down orbital asteroids with his Soul Gem ability. His Sky-Chi power, Mesozoic Mayhem, allows him to spin and demolish surrounding foes.

abilities.description: Do more damage with your Mace Smashes with an improved weapon!

abilities.name: Fault Zone
